verses.1:1: Now Moab revolted against Israel after Ahab died.
verses.1:2: And Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room that he had in Samaria and became sick; and he sent messengers, saying to them, "Go, consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, whether I can live through this illness of mine."
verses.1:3: But the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying, "Rise and go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and you will say to them, 'Is there no God in Israel, that you are going to consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron?
verses.1:4: Therefore this is what the Lord says: From the bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down, but you will surely die.'" And Elijah departed.
verses.1:5: And the messengers returned to Ahaziah. And he said to them, "Why have you returned?"
verses.1:6: And they answered him, "A man met us and said to us, 'Go and return to the king who sent you, and you will say to him, "This is what the Lord says: Is it because there was no God in Israel that you are sending to have Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, consulted? For that reason from the bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down, but you will surely die."'"
verses.1:7: And he said to them, "What is the appearance and dress of that man who met you and spoke these words?"
verses.1:8: And they said, "A hairy man, and bound around his waist with a leather belt." And he said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
verses.1:9: And he sent to him a captain of fifty, and the fifty who were under him. And he went up to him, and said to him as he sat on the summit of the mountain, "Man of God, the king has commanded that you come down."
verses.1:10: And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." And so fire came down from heaven and devoured him and the fifty who were with him.
verses.1:11: And again he sent to him a second captain of fifty, and fifty with him. And he spoke to him, "Man of God, this is what the king says: Hurry, come down."
verses.1:12: Elijah answered and said, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." Therefore fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
verses.1:13: Again he sent a third captain of fifty, and the fifty who were with him. And when he had come, he bent his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, and said, "Man of God, do not despise my life and the lives of your servants who are with me.
verses.1:14: Look, fire came down from heaven and devoured the first two captains of fifty and the fifties who were with them; but now I implore you to have mercy on my life."
verses.1:15: Then the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah, saying, "Go down with him; do not be afraid." Therefore he rose and went down with him to the king,
verses.1:16: and spoke to him, "This is what the Lord says: Because you sent messengers to consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel from whom you could inquire a word, therefore from the bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down, but you will surely die."
verses.1:17: So he died according to the word of the Lord that Elijah had spoken, and Joram his brother reigned in his place, in the second year of Joram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, for he had no son.
verses.1:18: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he performed, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.2:1: Now it happened, when the Lord willed to lift Elijah up by a whirlwind into heaven, that Elijah and Elisha were going from Gilgal.
verses.2:2: And Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel." And Elisha said to him, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you." And when they had gone down to Bethel,
verses.2:3: the sons of the prophets who were in Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the Lord will take your master away from you?" And he answered, "I know it too; be silent."
verses.2:4: Then Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you." And when they had come to Jericho,
verses.2:5: the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that the Lord will take your master away from you today?" And he said, "I know it too; be silent."
verses.2:6: Then Elijah said to him, "Stay here, because the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan." And he said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not abandon you." So both of them went together,
verses.2:7: and fifty men from the sons of the prophets followed them, who also stood opposite at a distance, while those two stood by the Jordan.
verses.2:8: And Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters, and they were divided to both sides, and both of them crossed over on dry ground.
verses.2:9: And when they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what you want me to do for you, before I am taken from you." And Elisha said, "I implore you, let your double spirit be in me."
verses.2:10: And he answered, "You have asked a difficult thing; nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, what you have asked for will be yours; but if you do not see me, it will not be."
verses.2:11: And as they proceeded on and conversed while walking, look, a fiery chariot and fiery horses separated the two of them, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
verses.2:12: And Elisha was watching and crying out, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its charioteer!" And he saw him no more; and he took hold of his own garments and tore them into two pieces.
verses.2:13: And he picked up the cloak of Elijah, which had fallen from him, and turning back, he stood on the bank of the Jordan,
verses.2:14: and with the cloak of Elijah, which had fallen from him, he struck the waters, and they were not divided; and he said, "Where is the God of Elijah even now?" And he struck the waters, and they were divided this way and that, and Elisha crossed over.
verses.2:15: Now when the sons of the prophets who were opposite in Jericho saw this, they said, "The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha." And coming to meet him, they bowed down to him, prostrate to the ground,
verses.2:16: and said to him, "Look, with your servants are fifty strong men who can go and search for your master, in case perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has taken him away and cast him onto one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." And he said, "Do not send them."
verses.2:17: And they pressed him until he consented and said, "Send them." And they sent fifty men, and when they had searched for three days, they did not find him.
verses.2:18: And they returned to him, while he was staying in Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not say to you, 'Do not send them'?"
verses.2:19: The men of the city also said to Elisha, "Look, the habitation of this city is very good, as you yourself, lord, clearly see; but the waters are very bad, and the land is barren."
verses.2:20: And he said, "Bring me a new vessel and put salt in it." And when they had brought it,
verses.2:21: he went out to the spring of the waters, threw salt into it, and said, "This is what the Lord says: I have healed these waters, and there will no longer be death or barrenness in them."
verses.2:22: Therefore the waters were healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
verses.2:23: And he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up along the road, little boys came out of the city and were mocking him, saying, "Go up, bald man! Go up, bald man!"
verses.2:24: And when he had looked back, he saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord; and two bears came out of the woods and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.
verses.2:25: And he departed from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
verses.3:1: Now Joram the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
verses.3:2: And he did evil before the Lord, though not like his father and mother; for he removed the statues of Baal that his father had made.
verses.3:3: Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, and did not turn away from them.
verses.3:4: Now Mesha, king of Moab, raised many flocks, and he used to pay to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs, and one hundred thousand rams with their fleeces.
verses.3:5: And when Ahab had died, he broke the covenant that he had with the king of Israel.
verses.3:6: Therefore King Joram went out from Samaria on that day and mustered all Israel.
verses.3:7: And he sent to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has withdrawn from me; come with me against him to battle." And he answered, "I will go up. He who is mine is yours; my people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
verses.3:8: And he said, "By which way will we go up?" And he answered, "Through the wilderness of Idumea."
verses.3:9: So the king of Israel, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out and went around on a seven-day journey, and there was no water for the army or for the beasts of burden that followed them.
verses.3:10: And the king of Israel said, "Alas! Alas! Alas! The Lord has gathered us three kings together to hand us over into the hands of Moab!"
verses.3:11: And Jehoshaphat said, "Is there a prophet of the Lord here, that we may pray to the Lord through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water over the hands of Elijah."
verses.3:12: And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the Lord is with him." And the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.3:13: But Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What is there between me and you? Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother." And the king of Israel said to him, "Why has the Lord gathered these three kings together to hand them over into the hands of Moab?"
verses.3:14: And Elisha said to him, "As the Lord of hosts lives, in whose sight I stand, if I did not respect the presence of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would not even have paid attention to you, nor looked at you.
verses.3:15: But now bring me a harpist." And while the harpist was playing, the hand of the Lord came upon him, and he said,
verses.3:16: "This is what the Lord says: Make the channel of this stream trenches and trenches.
verses.3:17: For this is what the Lord says: You will not see wind, nor rain, and this channel will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your households and your beasts of burden.
verses.3:18: And this is a small thing in the sight of the Lord; in addition, He will also hand Moab over into your hands.
verses.3:19: And you will strike every fortified city and every choice town, and you will cut down every fruit-bearing tree, and you will stop up all the springs of water, and you will cover every fine field with stones."
verses.3:20: So it happened in the morning, when the sacrifice is regularly offered, that, look, waters were coming by the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
verses.3:21: Now all the Moabites, hearing that the kings had come up to fight against them, summoned all who wore a sword belt from above, and they stood at the borders.
verses.3:22: And rising early in the morning, when the sun had already risen opposite the waters, the Moabites saw across from them the waters red like blood,
verses.3:23: and they said, "It is blood of the sword! The kings have fought against one another and have struck each other down; now go on to the plunder, Moab!"
verses.3:24: And they advanced into the camp of Israel; but rising up, Israel struck Moab, and they fled before them. Therefore those who had conquered came forward and struck Moab,
verses.3:25: and destroyed the cities; and they filled every finest field, each one throwing stones; and they stopped up all the springs of water; and they cut down all the fruit-bearing trees, so that only the clay walls remained; and the city was surrounded by slingers and struck in large part.
verses.3:26: And when the king of Moab saw this, namely, that the enemies had prevailed, he took with him seven hundred men drawing the sword to break through to the king of Edom, and they could not.
verses.3:27: And seizing his firstborn son, who was going to reign in his place, he offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And great indignation arose in Israel, and immediately they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.
verses.4:1: Now a certain woman of the wives of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared the Lord; and now the creditor has come to take my two sons to serve him."
verses.4:2: Elisha said to her, "What do you want me to do for you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?" And she answered, "I, your maidservant, have nothing in my house except a little oil with which to anoint myself."
verses.4:3: He said to her, "Go, borrow from all your neighbors empty vessels, not a few,
verses.4:4: and go inside and shut your door when you and your sons are within; and pour from it into all these vessels, and when they are full, you will take them away."
verses.4:5: So the woman went and shut the door on herself and on her sons; they kept bringing the vessels, and she kept pouring.
verses.4:6: And when the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me yet another vessel." And he answered, "I do not have any." And the oil stopped.
verses.4:7: Then she came and reported to the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil, and repay your creditor; and you and your sons, live on what remains."
verses.4:8: Now a certain day came, and Elisha was passing through Shunem; and there was a great woman there, who detained him to eat bread; and as he frequently passed by there, he would turn aside to her to eat bread.
verses.4:9: And she said to her husband, "I perceive that this man is a holy man of God, who passes by us frequently.
verses.4:10: Therefore let us make a small upper room for him, and let us place for him in it a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand, so that when he comes to us, he may stay there."
verses.4:11: So a certain day came, and coming by, he turned aside into the upper room and rested there.
verses.4:12: And he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." And when he had called her, and she stood before him,
verses.4:13: he said to his servant, "Speak to her: 'Look, you have diligently served us in all things; what do you want me to do for you? Do you have a matter of business, and do you want me to speak to the king or to the commander of the army?'" And she answered, "I dwell in the midst of my people."
verses.4:14: And he said, "What then does she want me to do for her?" And Gehazi said, "Do not ask; for she has no son, and her husband is old."
verses.4:15: So he commanded him to call her; and when she had been called and stood before the door,
verses.4:16: he said to her, "At this time, and at this same hour, if life accompanies us, you will have a son in your womb." And she answered, "Do not, I beg you, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your maidservant."
verses.4:17: And the woman conceived and gave birth to a son at the time and at the same hour that Elisha had said.
verses.4:18: Now the boy grew; and when a certain day came, and he had gone out to his father, to the reapers,
verses.4:19: he said to his father, "My head hurts, my head hurts!" And he said to a servant, "Pick him up and bring him to his mother."
verses.4:20: And when he had picked him up and brought him to his mother, she placed him on her knees until noon, and he died.
verses.4:21: Then she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door; and going out,
verses.4:22: she called her husband and said, "Please send with me one of the servants and a female donkey, so that I may run out to the man of God and return."
verses.4:23: He said to her, "For what reason are you going to him? Today is not the new moon, nor the Sabbath." And she answered, "I will go."
verses.4:24: And she saddled the female donkey and commanded the servant, "Drive on and hurry; do not delay me in going, and do this which I command you."
verses.4:25: Therefore she set out and came to the man of God to Mount Carmel; and when the man of God saw her across the way, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is that Shunammite woman.
verses.4:26: Go therefore to meet her and say to her, 'Is it going well with you, and with your husband, and with your son?'" And she answered, "It is well."
verses.4:27: And when she came to the man of God on the mountain, she grasped his feet; and Gehazi approached to move her away. And the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is in bitterness, and the Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me."
verses.4:28: And she said to him, "Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say to you, 'Do not deceive me'?"
verses.4:29: And he said to Gehazi, "Bind up your loins, take my staff in your hand, and go. If a man meets you, do not greet him; and if anyone greets you, do not answer him; and you will place my staff upon the face of the boy."
verses.4:30: But the mother of the boy said, "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." Therefore he rose and followed her.
verses.4:31: Now Gehazi had gone on ahead of them and had placed the staff upon the face of the boy, and there was no voice and no sensation; and he returned to meet him and reported to him, saying, "The boy has not risen."
verses.4:32: Therefore Elisha entered the house, and look, the boy was lying dead on his bed;
verses.4:33: and having gone in, he shut the door on himself and on the boy, and prayed to the Lord.
verses.4:34: And he climbed up and lay upon the boy, and placed his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and he bent himself over him, and the flesh of the boy grew warm.
verses.4:35: Then he turned back and walked about in the house, once back and forth; and he climbed up and lay upon him; and the boy yawned seven times and opened his eyes.
verses.4:36: Then he called Gehazi and said to him, "Call this Shunammite woman." Having been called, she entered to him. And he said, "Pick up your son."
verses.4:37: She came and fell at his feet, and bowed down upon the ground; and she picked up her son and went out.
verses.4:38: And Elisha returned to Gilgal. Now there was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were dwelling before him. And he said to one of his servants, "Put on the large pot and cook stew for the sons of the prophets."
verses.4:39: And one went out into the field to gather wild herbs; and he found something like a wild vine, and gathered from it bitter gourds of the field, and filled his cloak, and returning, he chopped them into the pot of stew; for he did not know what it was.
verses.4:40: So they poured it out for their companions to eat; and when they tasted from the stew, they cried out, saying, "Death is in the pot, man of God!" And they could not eat.
verses.4:41: But he said, "Bring flour." And when they had brought it, he put it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the crowd, so that they may eat." And there was no longer any bitterness in the pot.
verses.4:42: Now a certain man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing to the man of God loaves of the firstfruits, twenty barley loaves, and new grain in his bag. And he said, "Give it to the people, so that they may eat."
verses.4:43: And his attendant answered him, "How much is this, that I should set it before one hundred men?" Again he said, "Give it to the people, so that they may eat; for this is what the Lord says: 'They will eat, and there will be some left over.'"
verses.4:44: So he set it before them; and they ate, and there was some left over, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.5:1: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honored; for through him the Lord gave deliverance to Syria; and he was a mighty and wealthy man, yet a leper.
verses.5:2: Now raiders had gone out from Syria and had led away captive from the land of Israel a little girl, who was in the service of Naaman's wife;
verses.5:3: and she said to her mistress, "If only my master had been with the prophet who is in Samaria! Surely he would have cured him of the leprosy that he has."
verses.5:4: So Naaman went in to his master and reported to him, saying, "Thus and thus the girl from the land of Israel spoke."
verses.5:5: And the king of Syria said to him, "Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." And when he had set out and had taken with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand gold pieces, and ten changes of garments,
verses.5:6: he delivered the letter to the king of Israel in these words: "When you receive this letter, know that I have sent my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."
verses.5:7: And when the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his garments and said, "Am I a god, that I can kill and make alive, that this man has sent to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Take note and see that he is seeking pretexts against me."
verses.5:8: And when Elisha the man of God heard this, namely that the king of Israel had torn his garments, he sent to him, saying, "Why have you torn your garments? Let him come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel."
verses.5:9: So Naaman came with horses and chariots, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha;
verses.5:10: and Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will recover health, and you will be cleansed."
verses.5:11: Naaman became angry and began leaving, saying, "I thought that he would come out to me, and standing there would call upon the name of the Lord his God, and would touch the place of the leprosy with his hand, and cure me.
verses.5:12: Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel, so that I might wash in them and be cleansed?" So when he had turned around and was going away in indignation,
verses.5:13: his servants approached him and spoke to him, "Father, even if the prophet had told you some great thing, surely you ought to have done it; how much more now that he has said to you, 'Wash, and you will be cleansed'?"
verses.5:14: He went down and washed in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little boy, and he was cleansed.
verses.5:15: And returning to the man of God with his entire company, he came and stood before him, and said, "Truly I know that there is no other god in all the earth, except only in Israel. Therefore I beg you to accept a blessing from your servant."
verses.5:16: But he answered, "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it." And though he pressed him hard, he would not consent at all.
verses.5:17: And Naaman said, "As you wish; yet, I beg you, grant to me, your servant, that I may take a two-mule load of earth; for your servant will no longer offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice to foreign gods, except to the Lord.
verses.5:18: Now this alone is the thing about which you should plead with the Lord for your servant: when my master enters the temple of Rimmon to bow down, and as he leans upon my hand, if I bow down in the temple of Rimmon while he bows down in that same place, that the Lord may forgive me, your servant, for this matter."
verses.5:19: And he said to him, "Go in peace." Therefore he departed from him in the choice season of the earth.
verses.5:20: And Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, said, "My master has spared this Naaman the Syrian by not accepting from him the things he brought; as the Lord lives, I will run after him and take something from him."
verses.5:21: And Gehazi followed behind Naaman; and when he saw him running toward him, he leaped down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is everything well?"
verses.5:22: And he said, "All is well. My master has sent me to you, saying, 'Just now two young men have come to me from Mount Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets; give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.'"
verses.5:23: And Naaman said, "It is better that you accept two talents." And he pressed him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, along with two sets of garments, and placed them upon two of his servants, who carried them before him.
verses.5:24: And when he had arrived, already in the evening, he took them from their hand and stored them in the house; and he dismissed the men, and they departed.
verses.5:25: Then he himself went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said, "Where are you coming from, Gehazi?" And he answered, "Your servant did not go anywhere."
verses.5:26: But he said, "Was not my heart present when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Now therefore you have accepted silver, and you have accepted garments so that you may buy olive groves, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and servants, and maidservants.
verses.5:27: Yet the leprosy of Naaman will also cling to you and to your offspring forever." And he went out from him, leprous like snow.
verses.6:1: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live before you is too narrow for us.
verses.6:2: Let us go all the way to the Jordan, and let each one take a single piece of timber from the forest, so that we may build for ourselves a place there to live." And he said, "Go."
verses.6:3: And one of them said, "Come then, you too, with your servants." He answered, "I will come."
verses.6:4: And he went with them. And when they had come to the Jordan, they were cutting wood.
verses.6:5: Now it happened that when one had cut down a piece of timber, the iron of the axe fell into the water; and he cried out and said, "Alas! Alas! Alas, my lord! And I had borrowed this very thing."
verses.6:6: Then the man of God said, "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. So he cut off a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron floated,
verses.6:7: and he said, "Take it." And he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.6:8: Now the king of Syria was fighting against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "In such and such a place let us set an ambush."
verses.6:9: Therefore the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, "Be careful not to pass into that place, because the Syrians are in ambush there."
verses.6:10: Therefore the king of Israel sent to the place of which the man of God had told him, and occupied it beforehand, and guarded himself there not once or twice.
verses.6:11: And the heart of the king of Syria was troubled over this matter; and having summoned his servants, he said, "Why do you not tell me who is a traitor against me with the king of Israel?"
verses.6:12: And one of his servants said, "Not at all, my lord the king, but Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel all the words, whatever you speak in your private chamber."
verses.6:13: And he said to them, "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and capture him." And they reported to him, saying, "Look, he is in Dothan."
verses.6:14: Therefore he sent horses and chariots there, and the strength of the army; and when they had come by night, they surrounded the city.
verses.6:15: Now the attendant of the man of God, rising at dawn and going out, saw an army all around the city, and horses and chariots; and he reported to him, saying, "Alas! Alas! Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"
verses.6:16: But he answered, "Do not be afraid, for more are with us than with them."
verses.6:17: And when Elisha had prayed, he said, "Lord, open the eyes of this man, so that he may see." And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw; and look, the mountain was full of horses and fiery chariots all around Elisha.
verses.6:18: Then the enemies came down to him; and Elisha prayed to the Lord, saying, "Please strike this people with blindness." And the Lord struck them so that they could not see, according to the word of Elisha.
verses.6:19: Then Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, nor is this the city. Follow me, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." So he led them into Samaria.
verses.6:20: And when they had entered into Samaria, Elisha said, "Lord, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see." And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw that they were in the middle of Samaria.
verses.6:21: And the king of Israel said to Elisha, when he had seen them, "Shall I strike them, my father?"
verses.6:22: But he said, "You shall not strike them, for you did not capture them with your sword and bow so that you might strike them; rather, set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink, and go to their master."
verses.6:23: And a great preparation of food was set before them, and they ate and drank; and he sent them away, and they departed to their master. And the raiders of Syria no longer came into the land of Israel.
verses.6:24: Now it happened after these things that Ben-hadad king of Syria gathered his entire army, and went up and was besieging Samaria.
verses.6:25: And a great famine arose in Samaria, and it was besieged so long that a donkey's head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a fourth part of a kab of doves' dung for five pieces of silver.
verses.6:26: And as the king of Israel was passing along the wall, a certain woman cried out to him, saying, "Save me, my lord the king!"
verses.6:27: And he said, "The Lord does not save you; from where can I save you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?" And the king said to her, "What do you want?" And she answered,
verses.6:28: "This woman said to me, 'Give your son, so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
verses.6:29: So we cooked my son and ate him. And I said to her on the next day, 'Give your son, so that we may eat him.' But she hid her son."
verses.6:30: When the king had heard this, he tore his garments, and he was passing along the wall. And all the people saw the sackcloth with which he was clothed against his flesh underneath.
verses.6:31: And the king said, "May God do these things to me, and add these things as well, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat remains on him today."
verses.6:32: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. So he sent a man ahead; and before that messenger arrived, he said to the elders, "Do you know that this son of a murderer has sent so that my head may be cut off? Watch therefore: when the messenger comes, shut the door and do not allow him to enter; for look, the sound of his master's feet is behind him."
verses.6:33: While he was still speaking to them, the messenger who was coming to him appeared. And he said, "Look, so great an evil is from the Lord; what more shall I expect from the Lord?"
verses.7:1: Then Elisha said, "Hear the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord says: 'At this time tomorrow, a measure of fine flour will go for one stater, and two measures of barley for one stater, at the gate of Samaria.'"
verses.7:2: Then one of the commanders, on whose hand the king was leaning, answering the man of God, said, "Even if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, could what you are saying possibly be?" And he said, "You will see it with your own eyes, and you will not eat from it."
verses.7:3: Now there were four leprous men beside the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why do we want to stay here until we die?
verses.7:4: If we choose to enter the city, we will die of famine; and if we remain here, we must die. Come then, and let us desert to the camp of Syria: if they spare us, we will live; but if they choose to kill us, we will die nonetheless."
verses.7:5: So they rose in the evening to come to the camp of Syria. And when they had come to the beginning of the camp of Syria, they found no one there.
verses.7:6: For the Lord had caused a sound to be heard in the camp of Syria, of chariots and of horses and of a very great army; and they said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and of the Egyptians, and they have come upon us!"
verses.7:7: Therefore they rose and fled in the darkness, and abandoned their tents, and the horses and donkeys, in the camp, and fled, desiring only to save their own lives.
verses.7:8: So when those lepers had come to the beginning of the camp, they entered one tent and ate and drank, and took from there silver and gold and garments, and went away and hid them; and they returned again to another tent, and taking likewise from there, they hid them.
verses.7:9: And they said to one another, "We are not doing right, for this is a day of good news. If we remain silent and refuse to report it until morning, we will be charged with a crime. Come, let us go and report it in the king's court."
verses.7:10: And when they had come to the gate of the city, they told them, saying, "We went to the camp of Syria, and we found no person there, except horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents pitched."
verses.7:11: Therefore the gatekeepers went and reported it inside the king's palace.
verses.7:12: And he rose in the night and said to his servants, "I tell you what the Syrians have done to us: they know that we are suffering from famine, and for that reason they have gone out from the camp and are hiding in the fields, saying, 'When they have come out from the city, we will capture them alive, and then we will be able to enter the city.'"
verses.7:13: Then one of his servants answered, "Let us take the five horses that have remained in the city (because only they are left in the entire multitude of Israel, for the others have been consumed), and by sending them, we will be able to investigate."
verses.7:14: So they brought two horses, and the king sent them to the camp of the Syrians, saying, "Go and see."
verses.7:15: And they went after them all the way to the Jordan; and look, the entire road was full of garments and vessels that the Syrians had cast aside when they were thrown into confusion. And the messengers returned and told the king.
verses.7:16: And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria; and a measure of fine flour went for one stater, and two measures of barley for one stater, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.7:17: Now the king stationed at the gate that commander on whose hand he was leaning; and the crowd trampled him in the entrance of the gate, and he died, according to what the man of God had spoken when the king had come down to him.
verses.7:18: And it happened according to the word of the man of God that he had spoken to the king, when he said, "Two measures of barley will go for one stater, and a measure of fine flour for one stater, at this same time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria,"
verses.7:19: when that commander had answered the man of God and said, "Even if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, could what you are saying possibly happen?" And he said to him, "You will see it with your own eyes, and you will not eat from it."
verses.7:20: So it happened to him just as had been foretold, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.8:1: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had caused to live, saying, "Arise, go, you and your household, and live as a foreigner wherever you find a place; for the Lord has summoned a famine, and it will come upon the land for seven years."
verses.8:2: So she arose and did according to the word of the man of God; and going with her household, she lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for many days.
verses.8:3: And when the seven years had ended, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went out to appeal to the king for her house and for her fields.
verses.8:4: Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, the attendant of the man of God, saying, "Tell me all the great deeds that Elisha has done."
verses.8:5: And while he was telling the king how he had raised one who was dead, the woman whose son he had made alive appeared, crying out to the king for her house and for her fields. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha raised."
verses.8:6: And the king questioned the woman, and she told him. And the king appointed one eunuch for her, saying, "Restore to her everything that is hers, and all the revenues of the fields, from the day she left the land until the present."
verses.8:7: Elisha also came to Damascus, and Ben-hadad king of Syria was sick. And they reported to him, saying, "The man of God has come here."
verses.8:8: And the king said to Hazael, "Take gifts with you, and go to meet the man of God, and consult the Lord through him, saying, 'Will I be able to escape from this illness of mine?'"
verses.8:9: So Hazael went to meet him, having with him gifts and all the good things of Damascus, the loads of forty camels. And when he stood before him, he said, "Your son Ben-hadad, king of Syria, has sent me to you, saying, 'Will I be able to be healed from this illness of mine?'"
verses.8:10: And Elisha said to him, "Go, say to him, 'You will be healed.' Yet the Lord has shown me that he will certainly die."
verses.8:11: And he stood with him, and was troubled to the flushing of his face; and the man of God wept.
verses.8:12: Hazael said to him, "Why is my lord weeping?" And he said, "Because I know what evils you are about to do to the sons of Israel. You will burn their fortified cities with fire, and you will kill their young men with the sword, and you will crush their little ones, and you will split open the pregnant women."
verses.8:13: And Hazael said, "For what am I, your servant, a dog, that I should do this great thing?" And Elisha said, "The Lord has shown me that you will be king of Syria."
verses.8:14: When he had departed from Elisha, he came to his master. And he said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he answered, "He said to me, 'You will regain health.'"
verses.8:15: And when the next day had come, he took a blanket and poured water on it and spread it over his face; and when he had died, Hazael reigned in his place.
verses.8:16: In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, and of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, Joram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.8:17: He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.8:18: And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had walked, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord.
verses.8:19: Yet the Lord was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant, just as He had promised him, that He would give a lamp to him and to his sons for all days.
verses.8:20: In his days Edom broke away so as not to be under Judah, and appointed a king for itself.
verses.8:21: And Joram came to Zair, and all the chariots with him; and he arose by night and struck the Idumeans who had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots; but the people fled to their tents.
verses.8:22: Therefore Edom broke away so as not to be under Judah, until this day. Then Libnah also broke away at that time.
verses.8:23: Now the rest of the accounts of Joram, and everything that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.8:24: And Joram slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.8:25: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah, son of Joram king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.8:26: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.8:27: And he walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, and did what is evil before the Lord, just like the house of Ahab; for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
verses.8:28: He also went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.
verses.8:29: So he returned to be healed in Jezreel, because the Syrians had wounded him at Ramoth while he was fighting against Hazael king of Syria. Moreover, Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, went down to visit Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick there.
verses.9:1: Now Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your loins, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.9:2: And when you arrive there, you will see Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi; and going in, you will make him rise from the midst of his brothers, and you will bring him into an inner room.
verses.9:3: And holding the flask of oil, you will pour it on his head and say, 'This is what the Lord says: I have anointed you king over Israel.' And you will open the door and flee, and you will not linger there."
verses.9:4: So the young man, the attendant of the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead,
verses.9:5: and went in there; and look, the commanders of the army were sitting. And he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which one of all of us?" And he said, "For you, commander."
verses.9:6: And he arose and entered the room; and the other poured the oil on his head and said, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'I have anointed you king over the people of the Lord, Israel,
verses.9:7: and you will strike the house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the Lord from the hand of Jezebel.
verses.9:8: And I will destroy the entire house of Ahab, and I will kill from Ahab anyone who urinates against a wall, both the confined and the last in Israel.
verses.9:9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
verses.9:10: The dogs will also eat Jezebel in the field of Jezreel, and there will be no one to bury her.'" And he opened the door and fled.
verses.9:11: Now Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and they said to him, "Is everything well? Why did this madman come to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and what he spoke."
verses.9:12: But they answered, "It is false; rather, tell us." And he said to them, "He spoke this and that to me, and he said, 'This is what the Lord says: I have anointed you king over Israel.'"
verses.9:13: Therefore they hurried, and each one taking his cloak, they placed them under his feet in the likeness of a tribunal, and they blew the trumpet and said, "Jehu has become king!"
verses.9:14: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had besieged Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael king of Syria,
verses.9:15: and he had returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds, because the Syrians had struck him while he was fighting against Hazael king of Syria. And Jehu said, "If it pleases you, let no one go out as a fugitive from the city, so that he does not go and report in Jezreel."
verses.9:16: And he mounted up and set out for Jezreel; for Joram was sick there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to visit Joram.
verses.9:17: Now the watchman who was standing on the tower of Jezreel saw the troop of Jehu coming, and said, "I see a troop." And Joram said, "Take a chariot and send it to meet them, and let him say as he goes, 'Is everything well?'"
verses.9:18: So the one who had mounted the chariot went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is everything peaceful?'" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Pass over and follow me." The watchman also reported, saying, "The messenger came to them, and he is not returning."
verses.9:19: He also sent a second chariot of horses; and he came to them and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What have you to do with peace? Pass over and follow me."
verses.9:20: And the watchman reported, saying, "He came right up to them, and he is not returning; and the pace is like the pace of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he advances headlong."
verses.9:21: And Joram said, "Harness the chariot." And they harnessed his chariot, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his own chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu, and they found him in the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.9:22: And when Joram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he answered, "What peace? The fornications of Jezebel your mother and her many sorceries still flourish."
verses.9:23: Then Joram turned his hand, and fleeing, he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
verses.9:24: Then Jehu drew a bow with his hand and struck Joram between the shoulder blades; and the arrow went out through his heart, and immediately he collapsed in his chariot.
verses.9:25: And Jehu said to Bidkar the captain, "Pick him up, throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for I remember when you and I, sitting in a chariot, were following Ahab his father, that the Lord lifted up this burden against him, saying,
verses.9:26: 'Surely for the blood of Naboth and for the blood of his sons, which I saw yesterday,' says the Lord, 'I will repay you in this field,' says the Lord. Now therefore, pick him up and throw him into the field, according to the word of the Lord."
verses.9:27: Now Ahaziah king of Judah, seeing this, fled by the way of the garden house; and Jehu pursued him and said, "Strike him also in his chariot!" And they struck him at the ascent of Gaver, which is near Ibleam; and he fled to Megiddo and died there.
verses.9:28: And his servants placed him on his chariot and carried him to Jerusalem, and they buried him in a tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.9:29: In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah began to reign over Judah.
verses.9:30: And Jehu came to Jezreel. Now Jezebel, having heard of his arrival, painted her eyes with antimony, adorned her head, and looked out through the window
verses.9:31: at Jehu entering through the gate, and she said, "Can there be peace for Zimri, who killed his master?"
verses.9:32: And Jehu lifted his face toward the window and said, "Who is this woman?" And two or three eunuchs leaned down toward him.
verses.9:33: And he said to them, "Throw her down!" And they threw her down, and the wall was spattered with blood, and the hooves of the horses trampled her.
verses.9:34: And when he had gone in to eat and drink, he said, "Go and see to that cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
verses.9:35: And when they had gone to bury her, they found nothing except the skull, and the feet, and the ends of the hands.
verses.9:36: And returning, they reported to him. And Jehu said, "It is the word of the Lord, which He spoke through His servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the field of Jezreel the dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel,
verses.9:37: and the flesh of Jezebel will be like dung upon the face of the earth in the field of Jezreel, so that those passing by will say, "Is this that Jezebel?"'"
verses.10:1: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Therefore Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the nobles of the city, and to the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
verses.10:2: "As soon as you receive these letters, you who have the sons of your master, and chariots, and horses, and fortified cities, and weapons,
verses.10:3: choose the best one, and the one who pleases you from the sons of your master, and place him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master."
verses.10:4: They were greatly afraid and said, "Look, two kings could not stand before him, and how will we be able to resist?"
verses.10:5: Therefore the overseers of the house, and the governors of the city, and the elders, and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants; whatever you command we will do, nor will we appoint a king for ourselves; whatever pleases you, do it."
verses.10:6: Then he wrote letters back to them a second time, saying, "If you are mine and obey me, take the heads of the sons of your master and come to me at this same hour tomorrow in Jezreel." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were being brought up with the nobles of the city.
verses.10:7: And when the letters came to them, they took the king's sons and killed seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him in Jezreel.
verses.10:8: Then a messenger came and reported to him, saying, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." And he replied, "Place them in two heaps beside the entrance of the gate until morning."
verses.10:9: And when daylight came, he went out, and standing, said to all the people, "You are righteous; if I conspired against my master and killed him, who struck down all these?
verses.10:10: See therefore now that nothing of the words of the Lord has fallen to the ground, which the Lord spoke concerning the house of Ahab; and the Lord has done what He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah."
verses.10:11: Therefore Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his nobles, and acquaintances, and priests, until no remnant was left of him.
verses.10:12: And he arose and went to Samaria; and when he had come to the Chamber of the Shepherds on the way,
verses.10:13: he found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said to them, "Who are you?" And they answered, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen."
verses.10:14: And he said, "Seize them alive." And when they had seized them alive, they slaughtered them in the cistern beside the Chamber, forty-two men; and he did not leave any of them.
verses.10:15: And when he had departed from there, he found Jonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him, and he blessed him. And he said to him, "Is your heart right, just as my heart is with your heart?" And Jonadab said, "It is." "If it is," he said, "give me your hand." And he gave him his hand. And he lifted him up to himself into the chariot,
verses.10:16: and said to him, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord." And having placed him in his chariot,
verses.10:17: he brought him into Samaria. And he struck down all who had remained of Ahab in Samaria, down to the last one, according to the word of the Lord which He spoke through Elijah.
verses.10:18: Therefore Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab worshiped Baal a little, but I will worship him more.
verses.10:19: Now therefore, summon to me all the prophets of Baal, and all his servants, and all his priests; let there be no one who does not come, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing will not live." Now Jehu was doing this deceitfully, so that he might destroy the worshipers of Baal.
verses.10:20: And he said, "Sanctify a solemn day for Baal." And he proclaimed it,
verses.10:21: and sent throughout all the borders of Israel, and all the servants of Baal came; not even one remained who did not come. And they entered the temple of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from end to end.
verses.10:22: And he said to those who were over the garments, "Bring out vestments for all the servants of Baal." And they brought out garments for them.
verses.10:23: And Jehu and Jonadab the son of Rechab entered the temple of Baal, and he said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search carefully and see that none of the servants of the Lord happens to be with you, but only the servants of Baal."
verses.10:24: Therefore they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had prepared for himself eighty men outside and had said to them, "Whoever escapes from these men whom I bring into your hands, his life will be for the life of that one."
verses.10:25: And it happened, when the burnt offering had been completed, that Jehu commanded his soldiers and captains, "Go in and strike them down; let no one escape." And they struck them down with the edge of the sword, and the soldiers and captains cast them out, and went into the city of the temple of Baal,
verses.10:26: and brought out the statue from the shrine of Baal and burned it,
verses.10:27: and shattered it. They also destroyed the sanctuary of Baal, and made latrines in its place until this day.
verses.10:28: Thus Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel;
verses.10:29: nevertheless, he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, nor did he abandon the golden calves that were in Bethel and in Dan.
verses.10:30: And the Lord said to Jehu, "Because you have diligently done what was right and what was pleasing in My eyes, and have done all things that were in My heart against the house of Ahab, your sons to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."
verses.10:31: Yet Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart, for he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had made Israel sin.
verses.10:32: In those days the Lord began to grow weary of Israel; and Hazael struck them in all the borders of Israel,
verses.10:33: from the Jordan toward the eastern region, all the land of Gilead, and Gad, and Reuben, and Manasseh, from Aroer, which is by the brook Arnon, and Gilead, and Bashan.
verses.10:34: Now the rest of the words of Jehu, and all that he did, and his might, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.10:35: And Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:36: Now the days that Jehu reigned over Israel are twenty-eight years in Samaria.
verses.11:1: Now Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, seeing that her son was dead, arose and killed all the royal seed.
verses.11:2: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, taking Joash the son of Ahaziah, stole him from the midst of the king's sons who were being killed, and his nurse from the bedchamber, and she hid him from the face of Athaliah so that he would not be killed.
verses.11:3: And he was with her for six years secretly in the house of the Lord, while Athaliah reigned over the land.
verses.11:4: Now in the seventh year Jehoiada sent, and taking the centurions and the soldiers, he brought them in to himself into the temple of the Lord, and made a covenant with them; and putting them under oath in the house of the Lord, he showed them the king's son,
verses.11:5: and he commanded them, saying, "This is the word that you must carry out:
verses.11:6: let a third part of you come in on the Sabbath and keep the watch of the king's house. And let a third part be at the gate of Sur, and let a third part be at the gate that is behind the quarters of the shield-bearers; and you will keep the watch of the house of Messa.
verses.11:7: But let two parts of you, all who go out on the Sabbath, keep the watch of the house of the Lord around the king.
verses.11:8: And you will surround him, having weapons in your hands; and if anyone enters the enclosure of the temple, let him be killed; and you will be with the king as he comes in and goes out."
verses.11:9: And the centurions did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded them; and each one taking his men who were coming in on the Sabbath, together with those who were going out on the Sabbath, they came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.11:10: And he gave them the spears and weapons of King David, which were in the house of the Lord.
verses.11:11: And they stood, each one having weapons in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the altar and of the sanctuary, around the king.
verses.11:12: And he brought out the king's son, and placed on him the diadem and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him; and clapping their hands, they said, "Long live the king!"
verses.11:13: Now Athaliah heard the sound of the people running, and going in to the crowds in the temple of the Lord,
verses.11:14: she saw the king standing on the platform according to custom, and the singers and the trumpets near him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and sounding trumpets. And she tore her garments and cried out, "Conspiracy! Conspiracy!"
verses.11:15: Then Jehoiada commanded the centurions who were over the army and said to them, "Lead her out beyond the enclosures of the temple, and whoever follows her, let him be struck with the sword." For the priest had said, "Let her not be killed in the temple of the Lord."
verses.11:16: And they laid hands on her and drove her by way of the entrance of the horses, beside the palace, and she was killed there.
verses.11:17: Therefore Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they would be the people of the Lord, and between the king and the people.
verses.11:18: And all the people of the land entered the temple of Baal and destroyed his altars, and thoroughly crushed the images; they also killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altar. And the priest stationed guards in the house of the Lord.
verses.11:19: And he took the centurions, and the legions of the Cherethites and Pelethites, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord, and came by way of the gate of the shield-bearers into the palace; and he sat on the throne of the kings.
verses.11:20: And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; but Athaliah was killed with the sword in the king's house.
verses.12:1: And Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
verses.12:2: In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.
verses.12:3: And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jehoiada the priest taught him.
verses.12:4: Nevertheless, he did not remove the high places, for the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.12:5: And Joash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy things that is brought into the temple of the Lord by those who pass by, that is offered for the price of a soul, and that they bring into the temple of the Lord willingly and by the choice of their heart,
verses.12:6: let the priests receive it according to their order, and let them carry out the repairs of the house, if they see anything in need of restoration."
verses.12:7: Now up to the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not carried out the repairs of the temple.
verses.12:8: And King Joash called Jehoiada the high priest and the priests, saying to them, "Why are you not carrying out the repairs of the temple? Therefore, do not receive money any longer according to your order, but turn it over for the restoration of the temple."
verses.12:9: And the priests were prohibited from receiving money any further from the people and from carrying out the repairs of the house.
verses.12:10: And Jehoiada the high priest took one treasury chest, and opened a hole in the top, and placed it beside the altar on the right side of those entering the house of the Lord; and the priests who guarded the doors put into it all the money that was brought to the temple of the Lord.
verses.12:11: And when they saw that there was a very large amount of money in the treasury chest, the king's scribe and the high priest went up, and they poured out and counted the money that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.12:12: And they gave it according to number and measure into the hand of those who were in charge of the masons of the house of the Lord, who spent it on the carpenters and on the masons, those who worked in the house of the Lord
verses.12:13: and made the repairs, and on those who cut stones, and to buy timber and stones that were quarried, so that the restoration of the house of the Lord was completed in all things that needed expense to strengthen the house.
verses.12:14: Nevertheless, there were not made from that same money water jars of the temple of the Lord, or forks, or censers, or trumpets, or any vessel of gold and silver, from the money that was brought into the temple of the Lord.
verses.12:15: For it was given to those who were doing the work, so that the temple of the Lord might be restored.
verses.12:16: And no accounting was made with those men who received the money to distribute it to the craftsmen, but they handled it in good faith.
verses.12:17: But they did not bring the money for trespass and the money for sins into the temple of the Lord, because it belonged to the priests.
verses.12:18: Then Hazael king of Syria went up and fought against Gath, and captured it; and he set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: For this reason Joash king of Judah took all the sacred things that Jehoshaphat, and Joram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and those that he himself had offered, and all the silver that could be found in the treasuries of the temple of the Lord and in the king's palace, and sent them to Hazael king of Syria; and he withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.12:20: Now the rest of the accounts of Joash, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.12:21: And his servants rose up and conspired among themselves, and struck Joash in the house of Millo, on the descent of Silla.
verses.12:22: For Jozacar the son of Shimeath and Jozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years.
verses.13:2: And he did evil before the Lord, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, and he did not turn aside from them.
verses.13:3: And the fury of the Lord was enraged against Israel, and He handed them over into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, all the days.
verses.13:4: Now Jehoahaz implored the face of the Lord, and the Lord heard him; for He saw the distress of Israel, because the king of Syria had crushed them.
verses.13:5: And the Lord gave a savior to Israel, and Israel was delivered from the hand of the king of Syria; and the sons of Israel lived in their tents as yesterday and the day before yesterday.
verses.13:6: Nevertheless, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin, but walked in them; indeed, even the sacred grove remained in Samaria.
verses.13:7: And none were left to Jehoahaz from the people except fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers; for the king of Syria had killed them and had reduced them like dust in the threshing of a threshing floor.
verses.13:8: Now the rest of the accounts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:9: And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Joash the son of Jehoahaz reigned over Israel in Samaria for sixteen years.
verses.13:11: And he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, but walked in them.
verses.13:12: Now the rest of the accounts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might, how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:13: And Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne. Moreover, Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.13:14: Now Elisha was sick with the illness from which he also died; and Joash king of Israel went down to him, and wept before him, and said, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its charioteer!"
verses.13:15: And Elisha said to him, "Bring a bow and arrows." And when he had brought a bow and arrows to him,
verses.13:16: he said to the king of Israel, "Place your hand upon the bow." And when he had placed his hand, Elisha placed his hands over the hands of the king,
verses.13:17: and said, "Open the eastern window." And when he had opened it, Elisha said, "Shoot an arrow." And he shot. And Elisha said, "The arrow of the Lord's salvation, and the arrow of salvation against Syria; and you will strike Syria in Aphek until you consume it."
verses.13:18: And he said, "Take the arrows." And when he had taken them, he said to him again, "Strike the ground with an arrow." And when he had struck three times and stopped,
verses.13:19: the man of God became angry with him and said, "If you had struck five times, or six times, or seven times, you would have struck Syria to complete destruction; but now you will strike it three times."
verses.13:20: So Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiders from Moab came into the land in that very year.
verses.13:21: And some men who were burying a man saw the raiders, and threw the corpse into the tomb of Elisha. And when it touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood upon his feet.
verses.13:22: Now Hazael king of Syria afflicted Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.13:23: And the Lord had mercy on them and turned back to them because of His covenant, which He had with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob; and He was not willing to destroy them, nor to cast them away completely up to the present time.
verses.13:24: And Hazael king of Syria died, and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:25: Moreover, Joash the son of Jehoahaz took the cities from the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, which he had taken from the hand of Jehoahaz his father by right of battle; three times Joash struck him, and he restored the cities of Israel.
verses.14:1: In the second year of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.14:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
verses.14:3: And he did what was right before the Lord, yet not like his father David. He did according to all that his father Joash had done,
verses.14:4: except only this, that he did not remove the high places; for the people were still offering sacrifices and burning incense on the high places.
verses.14:5: And when he had secured the kingdom, he struck down his servants who had killed the king, his father.
verses.14:6: However, he did not kill the sons of those who had killed, according to what is written in the book of the law of Moses, just as the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers will not die for sons, nor will sons die for fathers; rather, each one will die in his own sin."
verses.14:7: He himself struck down ten thousand of Edom in the Valley of the Salt Pits, and seized the rock in battle, and called its name Joktheel, to the present day.
verses.14:8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Joash, son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, and let us see one another."
verses.14:9: And Joash, king of Israel, sent back to Amaziah, king of Judah, saying, "The thistle of Lebanon sent to the cedar that is in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' And the beasts of the forest that are in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
verses.14:10: By striking, you have prevailed over Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be content with glory, and stay in your house; why do you provoke disaster, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
verses.14:11: And Amaziah did not consent. So Joash, king of Israel, went up, and they saw one another, he and Amaziah, king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, a town of Judah.
verses.14:12: And Judah was struck down before Israel, and they fled, each one to his tents.
verses.14:13: Now Joash, king of Israel, captured Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he breached the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, for four hundred cubits.
verses.14:14: And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king, and hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.14:15: Now the rest of the accounts of Joash, what he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah, king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:16: And Joash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
verses.14:17: Now Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, died.
verses.14:18: Now the rest of the accounts of Amaziah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:19: And a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, but he fled to Lachish. And they sent after him to Lachish, and killed him there.
verses.14:20: And they carried him away on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.14:21: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and appointed him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.14:22: He himself built Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his fathers.
verses.14:23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam, son of Joash, king of Israel, reigned in Samaria for forty-one years.
verses.14:24: And he did what is evil before the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.14:25: He himself restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the Sea of the Wilderness, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel which He spoke through His servant Jonah, son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath, which is in Opher.
verses.14:26: For the Lord saw the exceedingly bitter affliction of Israel, and that they had been consumed even to those shut up in prison and the lowest, and that there was no one to help Israel.
verses.14:27: Nor did the Lord say that He would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, but He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam, son of Joash.
verses.14:28: Now the rest of the accounts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might with which he waged war, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah in Israel, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:29: And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah, son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:2: He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
verses.15:3: And he did what was pleasing before the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
verses.15:4: Yet he did not demolish the high places; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.15:5: Now the Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived in a free house apart; while Jotham, the king's son, governed the palace and would judge the people of the land.
verses.15:6: Now the rest of the accounts of Azariah, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:7: And Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his ancestors in the city of David, and his son Jotham reigned in his place.
verses.15:8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zechariah, son of Jeroboam, reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months.
verses.15:9: And he did what is evil before the Lord, just as his fathers had done; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.15:10: Now Shallum, son of Jabesh, conspired against him, and struck him openly and killed him, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:11: Now the rest of the accounts of Zechariah, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:12: This is the word of the Lord which He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Your sons to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel." And so it happened.
verses.15:13: Shallum, son of Jabesh, began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah, and he reigned for one month in Samaria.
verses.15:14: And Menahem, son of Gadi, went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and struck Shallum, son of Jabesh, in Samaria, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:15: Now the rest of the accounts of Shallum, and his conspiracy by which he laid an ambush, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:16: Then Menahem struck Tiphsah and all who were in it, and its borders from Tirzah, for they had refused to open to him; and he killed all its pregnant women and ripped them open.
verses.15:17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Menahem, son of Gadi, reigned over Israel for ten years in Samaria.
verses.15:18: And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin, all his days.
verses.15:19: Pul, king of the Assyrians, was coming into the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, so that he would be a help to him and strengthen his kingdom.
verses.15:20: And Menahem levied the silver upon Israel, upon all the powerful and wealthy, so that he might give to the king of the Assyrians fifty shekels of silver per person; and the king of the Assyrians turned back and did not stay in the land.
verses.15:21: Now the rest of the accounts of Menahem, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:22: And Menahem slept with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigned in his place.
verses.15:23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekahiah, son of Menahem, reigned over Israel in Samaria for two years.
verses.15:24: And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.15:25: Now Pekah, son of Remaliah, his commander, conspired against him and struck him in Samaria in the tower of the royal house, beside Argob and beside Arieh, and with him fifty men from the sons of the Gileadites; and he killed him and reigned in his place.
verses.15:26: Now the rest of the accounts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekah, son of Remaliah, reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty years.
verses.15:28: And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
verses.15:29: In the days of Pekah, king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, came and captured Ijon, and Abel House, Maacah and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, and carried them away to the Assyrians.
verses.15:30: Now Hoshea, son of Elah, conspired and laid an ambush against Pekah, son of Remaliah, and struck him and killed him, and reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham, son of Uzziah.
verses.15:31: Now the rest of the accounts of Pekah, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:32: In the second year of Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:33: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.
verses.15:34: And he did what was pleasing before the Lord; he acted according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
verses.15:35: Yet he did not remove the high places; the people were still offering sacrifices and burning incense on the high places. He himself built the highest gate of the house of the Lord.
verses.15:36: Now the rest of the accounts of Jotham, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:37: In those days the Lord began to send Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, against Judah.
verses.15:38: And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David, his father; and his son Ahaz reigned in his place.
verses.16:1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, became king.
verses.16:2: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was pleasing in the sight of the Lord his God, as David his father did,
verses.16:3: but he walked in the way of the kings of Israel; moreover, he even consecrated his son, passing him through the fire according to the idols of the nations, which the Lord destroyed before the sons of Israel.
verses.16:4: He also sacrificed victims and burned incense on the high places, and on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
verses.16:5: Then Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to fight; and when they besieged Ahaz, they were not able to overcome him.
verses.16:6: At that time Rezin, king of Syria, restored Elath to Syria and drove out the Judeans from Elath; and the Edomites came into Elath and lived there to this day.
verses.16:7: Now Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser, king of the Assyrians, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who have risen up against me."
verses.16:8: And when he had gathered the silver and gold that could be found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king, he sent gifts to the king of the Assyrians.
verses.16:9: And he consented to his wish; for the king of the Assyrians went up against Damascus and laid it waste, and deported its inhabitants to Cyrene, and he put Rezin to death.
verses.16:10: And King Ahaz proceeded to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of the Assyrians; and when he had seen the altar of Damascus, King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest a pattern of it and a likeness according to all its workmanship.
verses.16:11: And Uriah the priest built an altar; according to all that King Ahaz had commanded from Damascus, so Uriah the priest did until King Ahaz came from Damascus.
