verses.16:12: And when the king had come from Damascus, he saw the altar and venerated it; and he went up and offered burnt offerings and his sacrifice,
verses.16:13: and poured out drink offerings, and poured upon the altar the blood of the peace offerings that he had offered.
verses.16:14: Moreover, the bronze altar that was before the Lord he moved from the front of the temple, and from the place of the altar, and from the place of the temple of the Lord; and he placed it on the side of the altar toward the north.
verses.16:15: King Ahaz also commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "Upon the greater altar offer the morning burnt offering and the evening sacrifice, and the burnt offering of the king and his sacrifice, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land and their sacrifices and their drink offerings; and all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrificial victim you shall pour out upon it; but the bronze altar shall be ready according to my will."
verses.16:16: So Uriah the priest did according to everything that King Ahaz had commanded.
verses.16:17: Now King Ahaz removed the carved bases and the basin that was on top; and he took down the sea from the bronze oxen that supported it, and placed it upon a pavement laid with stone.
verses.16:18: Also the Musach of the Sabbath, which he had built in the temple, and the outer entrance of the king he turned into the temple of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.
verses.16:19: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.16:20: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David; and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.17:1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz, king of Judah, Hoshea, son of Elah, reigned in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
verses.17:2: And he did evil before the Lord, yet not like the kings of Israel who had been before him.
verses.17:3: Against him Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, went up, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.
verses.17:4: And when the king of the Assyrians discovered that Hoshea, striving to rebel, had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, so that he would not pay tribute to the king of the Assyrians as he had been accustomed to do each year, he besieged him and sent him bound into prison.
verses.17:5: And he traversed the whole land, and going up to Samaria, he besieged it for three years.
verses.17:6: Now in the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians; and he placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river Gozan, in the cities of the Medes.
verses.17:7: For it happened that when the sons of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, they worshiped foreign gods.
verses.17:8: And they walked according to the rite of the nations whom the Lord had consumed in the sight of the sons of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, because they had done likewise.
verses.17:9: And the sons of Israel offended the Lord their God with things that were not right; and they built for themselves high places in all their towns, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
verses.17:10: And they made for themselves statues and groves on every high hill and under every shady tree,
verses.17:11: and there they burned incense upon altars in the manner of the nations whom the Lord had removed from their presence; and they did most wicked things, provoking the Lord.
verses.17:12: And they worshiped impurities, concerning which the Lord commanded them not to do this thing.
verses.17:13: And the Lord testified against Israel and against Judah through the hand of all the prophets and seers, saying, "Turn back from your most wicked ways, and keep My precepts and ceremonies, according to all the law that I commanded your fathers, and as I sent to you by the hand of My servants the prophets."
verses.17:14: Yet they did not listen, but hardened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who refused to obey the Lord their God.
verses.17:15: And they rejected His ordinances, and the covenant that He made with their fathers, and the testimonies with which He bore witness to them; and they followed vanities and acted vainly, and they followed the nations that were all around them, concerning whom the Lord had commanded them that they should not do as those also did.
verses.17:16: And they abandoned all the precepts of the Lord their God, and made for themselves two cast calves and groves, and bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal,
verses.17:17: and consecrated their sons and their daughters through the fire; and they devoted themselves to divinations and auguries, and gave themselves over to do evil before the Lord, so as to provoke Him.
verses.17:18: And the Lord was intensely angry with Israel, and removed them from His sight, and none remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.17:19: Yet not even Judah itself kept the commandments of the Lord its God, but walked in the errors of Israel, which it had practiced.
verses.17:20: And the Lord cast off all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of plunderers, until He cast them out from His presence,
verses.17:21: already from that time when Israel was torn away from the house of David, and they appointed Jeroboam, son of Nebat, as king for themselves; for Jeroboam separated Israel from the Lord and caused them to sin a great sin.
verses.17:22: And the sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam that he had committed, and they did not depart from them,
verses.17:23: until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, just as He had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets; and Israel was deported from its own land to the Assyrians, to this day.
verses.17:24: Now the king of the Assyrians brought people from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Avva, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel; and they took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
verses.17:25: And when they began to live there, they did not fear the Lord; and the Lord sent lions among them, which were killing them.
verses.17:26: And it was reported to the king of the Assyrians, and it was said, "The nations that you deported and caused to live in the cities of Samaria do not know the ordinances of the God of the land; and the Lord has sent lions among them, and look, they are killing them, because they do not know the rite of the God of the land."
verses.17:27: Then the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, "Lead to that place one of the priests whom you brought captive from there, and let him go and live with them, and let him teach them the ordinances of the God of the land."
verses.17:28: Therefore, when one of these priests who had been led away captive from Samaria arrived, he lived in Bethel and taught them how they should worship the Lord.
verses.17:29: And each nation crafted its own god, and they placed them in the high shrines that the Samaritans had made, nation by nation in its own towns in which it lived.
verses.17:30: For the Babylonian men made Succoth-benoth, and the Cuthite men made Nergal, and the men from Hamath made Ashima.
verses.17:31: Moreover, the Hivites made Nibhaz and Tartak. And those who were from Sepharvaim burned their sons with fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim,
verses.17:32: and nevertheless they worshiped the Lord. Moreover, they made for themselves priests of the high places from among the lowest, and placed them in the lofty shrines.
verses.17:33: And while they worshiped the Lord, they also served their own gods according to the custom of the nations from which they had been deported to Samaria.
verses.17:34: To the present day they follow the ancient custom: they do not fear the Lord, nor do they keep His ceremonies, judgments, and law, and the commandment that the Lord had commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He surnamed Israel;
verses.17:35: and He had made a covenant with them and had commanded them, saying, "Do not fear foreign gods, and do not bow down to them, nor worship them, and do not sacrifice to them;
verses.17:36: but the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt with great strength and with an outstretched arm: fear Him, and bow down to Him, and sacrifice to Him.
verses.17:37: Also observe the ceremonies, and the judgments, and the law, and the commandment that He wrote for you, so as to do them all the days; and do not fear foreign gods.
verses.17:38: And do not forget the covenant that He made with you, nor worship foreign gods,
verses.17:39: but fear the Lord your God, and He Himself will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
verses.17:40: Yet they did not listen, but continued to act according to their former custom.
verses.17:41: So these nations were indeed fearing the Lord, yet nevertheless also serving their own idols; for both their sons and their grandsons, just as their fathers did, so they do to the present day.
verses.18:1: In the third year of Hoshea, son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
verses.18:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
verses.18:3: And he did what was good before the Lord, according to all that David his father had done.
verses.18:4: He himself destroyed the high places, and shattered the statues, and cut down the groves, and broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, since up to that time the sons of Israel were burning incense to it; and he called its name Nehushtan.
verses.18:5: He hoped in the Lord God of Israel; therefore, after him there was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, nor even among those who were before him.
verses.18:6: And he clung to the Lord, and he did not depart from His footsteps, and he carried out His commandments, which the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.18:7: For this reason the Lord was also with him, and in everything to which he went forth, he conducted himself wisely. He also rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
verses.18:8: He himself struck the Philistines as far as Gaza and all their borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
verses.18:9: In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea, son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, went up against Samaria and besieged it,
verses.18:10: and captured it. For after three years, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that is, in the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
verses.18:11: And the king of the Assyrians carried Israel away to the Assyrians, and settled them in Halah and in Habor, the rivers of Gozan, in the cities of the Medes,
verses.18:12: because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed His covenant; all that Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded, they neither listened to nor did.
verses.18:13: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, went up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
verses.18:14: Then Hezekiah, king of Judah, sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish, saying, "I have sinned; depart from me, and everything that you impose on me, I will bear." Therefore the king of the Assyrians levied on Hezekiah, king of Judah, three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.18:15: And Hezekiah gave all the silver that had been found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king.
verses.18:16: At that time Hezekiah broke off the doors of the temple of the Lord and the plates of gold that he himself had fastened, and he gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:17: Now the king of the Assyrians sent Tartan, and Rabsaris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem with a strong force. And when they had gone up, they came to Jerusalem, and they stood beside the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is on the road of the Fuller's Field.
verses.18:18: And they called for the king, but Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, overseer of the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, son of Asaph, keeper of the records, went out to them.
verses.18:19: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Speak to Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of the Assyrians, says: What is this confidence on which you rely?
verses.18:20: Perhaps you have formed a plan to prepare yourself for battle. In whom do you trust, that you dare to rebel?
verses.18:21: Or do you hope in a broken reed staff, Egypt, on which, if a man leans, it will splinter and enter his hand and pierce it? So is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.'
verses.18:22: But if you say to me, 'We have confidence in the Lord our God,' is not He the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, 'Before this altar you will worship in Jerusalem'?
verses.18:23: Now therefore, come over to my lord, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, and see whether you are able to have riders for them.
verses.18:24: And how can you resist before a single satrap of the least of my lord's servants? Or do you have confidence in Egypt because of chariots and horsemen?
verses.18:25: Have I indeed come up against this place without the will of the Lord to demolish it? The Lord said to me, 'Go up against this land and demolish it.'"
verses.18:26: Then Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, and Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "We ask that you speak to us, your servants, in Syriac, since we understand this language, and do not speak to us in Judean while the people who are on the wall are listening."
verses.18:27: And Rabshakeh answered them, saying, "Was it really to your lord and to you that my lord sent me to speak these words, and not rather to the men who are sitting on the wall, so that they may eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?"
verses.18:28: Therefore Rabshakeh stood and cried out with a loud voice in Judean, and said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of the Assyrians.
verses.18:29: This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah mislead you, for he will not be able to rescue you from my hand,
verses.18:30: nor let him give you confidence in the Lord, saying, 'Rescuing us, the Lord will deliver us, and this city will not be handed over into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.'
verses.18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah. For this is what the king of the Assyrians says: Do with me what is advantageous to you, and come out to me, and each one will eat from his own vine and from his own fig tree, and you will drink water from your own cisterns,
verses.18:32: until I come and carry you away to a land that is like your own land, to a fruitful land and fertile in wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and oil and honey; and you will live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, who deceives you, saying, 'The Lord will deliver us.'
verses.18:33: Have the gods of the nations delivered their land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
verses.18:34: Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? Where is the god of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
verses.18:35: Who are they among all the gods of the lands who have rescued their region from my hand, that the Lord should be able to rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"
verses.18:36: Therefore the people kept silent and did not answer him anything, since they had received the king's command that they should not answer him.
verses.18:37: And Eliakim, son of Hilkiah, overseer of the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, son of Asaph, keeper of the records, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
verses.19:1: When King Hezekiah heard these things, he tore his garments and covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the Lord.
verses.19:2: And he sent Eliakim, the overseer of the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders among the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.19:3: They said, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'This day is a day of distress, of rebuke, and of blasphemy; children have come to the point of birth, and the woman in labor has no strength.
verses.19:4: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of the Assyrians, his master, sent to reproach the living God and to reprove with words that the Lord your God has heard; and offer a prayer for the remnant that is found.'"
verses.19:5: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.19:6: And Isaiah said to them, "You will say this to your master: 'This is what the Lord says: "Do not be afraid in the face of the words that you have heard, with which the young men of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed Me.
verses.19:7: Look, I will put a spirit in him, and he will hear a report, and he will return to his own land; and I will bring him down by the sword in his own land."'"
verses.19:8: So Rabshakeh returned and found the king of the Assyrians attacking Libnah, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
verses.19:9: And when he had heard them saying concerning Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, "Look, he has come out to fight against you," and was going against him, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.19:10: "Say this to Hezekiah, king of Judah: 'Do not let your God, in whom you have confidence, deceive you, nor say, "Jerusalem will not be handed over into the hands of the king of the Assyrians."
verses.19:11: For you yourself have heard what the kings of the Assyrians have done to all the lands, how they have devastated them; will you alone, then, be able to be delivered?
verses.19:12: Have the gods of the nations delivered each of those whom my fathers devastated, namely Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
verses.19:13: Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?'"
verses.19:14: Therefore, when Hezekiah had received the letters from the hand of the messengers and had read them, he went up into the house of the Lord and spread them out before the Lord,
verses.19:15: and prayed in His sight, saying, "Lord, God of Israel, who sit above the cherubim, You alone are God of all the kings of the earth; You have made heaven and earth.
verses.19:16: Incline Your ear and hear; open Your eyes, Lord, and see; hear all the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to reproach the living God to us.
verses.19:17: Truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the nations and the lands of them all.
verses.19:18: And they cast their gods into the fire, for they were not gods, but the works of the hands of men, of wood and stone; and they destroyed them.
verses.19:19: Now therefore, Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the Lord God."
verses.19:20: Then Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sent to Hezekiah, saying, "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: 'What you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, I have heard.'
verses.19:21: This is the word that the Lord has spoken concerning him: 'The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and mocked you; the daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head behind your back.
verses.19:22: Whom have you reproached, and whom have you blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel.
verses.19:23: By the hand of your servants you have reproached the Lord, and you have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the summit of Lebanon, and I have cut down its tall cedars and its choice fir trees. And I have entered up to its borders, and the forest of its Carmel
verses.19:24: I myself have cut down. And I have drunk foreign waters, and with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the enclosed waters."
verses.19:25: Have you not heard what I have done from the beginning? From ancient days I formed it, and now I have brought it about; and fortified cities will become a ruin of fighting hills.
verses.19:26: And those who dwell in them, weak of hand, trembled and were put to shame; they became like the grass of the field and the green vegetation of the rooftops, which dried up before it came to maturity.
verses.19:27: Your dwelling place, and your going out, and your coming in, and your way I have known beforehand, and your fury against Me.
verses.19:28: You have raged against Me, and your arrogance has come up into My ears; therefore I will put a ring in your nostrils and a bit in your lips, and I will lead you back on the way by which you came.
verses.19:29: And to you, Hezekiah, this will be the sign: eat this year what you find; and in the second year, what grows of its own accord; moreover, in the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
verses.19:30: And whatever remains of the house of Judah will send root downward and bear fruit upward.
verses.19:31: For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and that which is saved from Mount Zion; the zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.'
verses.19:32: Therefore this is what the Lord says concerning the king of the Assyrians: 'He will not enter this city, nor shoot an arrow into it, nor will a shield seize it, nor will a siegework surround it.
verses.19:33: By the way by which he came, he will return, and he will not enter this city,' says the Lord.
verses.19:34: 'And I will protect this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"
verses.19:35: So it happened on that night that the angel of the Lord came and struck down in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred eighty-five thousand. And when he had risen at daybreak, he saw all the bodies of the dead; and departing, he went away,
verses.19:36: and Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, returned and remained in Nineveh.
verses.19:37: And while he was worshiping Nisroch his god in the temple, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword and fled into the land of the Armenians; and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
verses.20:1: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death; and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said to him, "This is what the Lord God says: 'Give instructions to your household, for you will die and will not live.'"
verses.20:2: Then he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord, saying,
verses.20:3: "I implore You, Lord, please remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done what is pleasing before You." And so Hezekiah wept with great weeping.
verses.20:4: And before Isaiah had gone out from the middle part of the courtyard, the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
verses.20:5: "Go back and say to Hezekiah, the leader of My people: 'This is what the Lord, the God of David your father, says: "I have heard your prayer, and I have seen your tears, and look, I have healed you; on the third day you will go up to the temple of the Lord.
verses.20:6: And I will add fifteen years to your days; moreover, I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and I will protect this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant."'"
verses.20:7: And Isaiah said, "Bring a cake of figs." And when they had brought it and placed it on his boil, he was cured.
verses.20:8: Now Hezekiah had said to Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the Lord will heal me, and that I will go up to the temple of the Lord on the third day?"
verses.20:9: Isaiah said to him, "This will be the sign from the Lord that the Lord will carry out the word that He has spoken: do you want the shadow to go up ten lines, or to return as many degrees?"
verses.20:10: And Hezekiah said, "It is easy for the shadow to grow by ten lines; I do not want this to happen, but rather for it to return backward by ten degrees."
verses.20:11: Therefore Isaiah the prophet called upon the Lord, and he brought the shadow back along the lines by which it had already gone down on the sundial of Ahaz, backward by ten degrees.
verses.20:12: At that time Berodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of the Babylonians, sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.
verses.20:13: And Hezekiah rejoiced at their arrival, and he showed them the house of aromatics, and the gold and the silver, and various spices, and ointments as well, and the house of his vessels, and everything that he could have in his treasuries. There was nothing that Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.
verses.20:14: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say? Or from where did they come to you?" Hezekiah said to him, "They came to me from a distant land, from Babylon."
verses.20:15: And he replied, "What have they seen in your house?" Hezekiah said, "They have seen everything that is in my house; there is nothing that I have not shown them in my treasuries."
verses.20:16: Therefore Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord:
verses.20:17: 'Look, days will come, and everything that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon; nothing will remain,' says the Lord.
verses.20:18: 'Moreover, some of your sons who will come from you, whom you will father, will be taken away, and they will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"
verses.20:19: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the Lord that you have spoken is good; let there be peace and truth in my days."
verses.20:20: Now the rest of the accounts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he made the pool and the aqueduct and brought the waters into the city, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.20:21: And Hezekiah slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Hephzibah.
verses.21:2: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the idols of the nations that the Lord destroyed from before the face of the sons of Israel.
verses.21:3: And he turned back and built the high places that Hezekiah his father had demolished; and he erected altars for Baal, and made groves just as Ahab king of Israel had done, and worshiped all the host of heaven and served it.
verses.21:4: And he constructed altars in the house of the Lord, concerning which the Lord said, "In Jerusalem I will place My name."
verses.21:5: And he constructed altars for the entire host of heaven in the two courts of the temple of the Lord.
verses.21:6: And he led his son through the fire, and practiced soothsaying, and observed omens, and appointed mediums, and multiplied diviners, so as to do evil before the Lord and provoke Him.
verses.21:7: He also placed the idol of the grove, which he had made, in the temple of the Lord, concerning which the Lord spoke to David and to Solomon his son: "In this temple and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will place My name forever.
verses.21:8: And I will no longer cause the foot of Israel to be moved from the land that I gave to their fathers, if only they observe in practice all that I have commanded them, and the entire law that My servant Moses enjoined on them."
verses.21:9: Yet they did not listen, but were led astray by Manasseh to do evil beyond the nations that the Lord crushed from before the face of the sons of Israel.
verses.21:10: And the Lord spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets, saying,
verses.21:11: "Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these most wicked abominations, beyond all that the Amorites did before him, and has also made Judah sin in his impurities,
verses.21:12: therefore this is what the Lord God of Israel says: Look, I will bring evils upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that whoever hears, both of his ears will tingle.
verses.21:13: And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab; and I will erase Jerusalem just as tablets are usually erased, and while erasing I will turn it and draw the stylus repeatedly over its face.
verses.21:14: And I will abandon the remnant of My inheritance and deliver them into the hands of its enemies, and they will become a desolation and a plunder for all their adversaries,
verses.21:15: because they have done evil before Me and have persisted in provoking Me, from the day on which their fathers went out from Egypt up to this day."
verses.21:16: Moreover, Manasseh also shed exceedingly much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem up to the mouth, apart from his sins by which he made Judah sin, to do evil before the Lord.
verses.21:17: Now the rest of the words of Manasseh, such as all that he did, and his sin that he sinned, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:18: And Manasseh slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son reigned in his place.
verses.21:19: Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; he also reigned two years in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
verses.21:20: And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as Manasseh his father had done.
verses.21:21: And he walked in the entire way along which his father had walked, and he served the impurities that his father had served, and worshiped them;
verses.21:22: and he abandoned the Lord God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the Lord.
verses.21:23: And his servants laid an ambush for him, and killed the king in his house.
verses.21:24: However, the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and they appointed Josiah his son as king for themselves in his place.
verses.21:25: Now the rest of the words of Amon, what he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:26: And they buried him in his tomb, in the garden of Uzza; and Josiah his son reigned in his place.
verses.22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign; he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
verses.22:2: And he did what was pleasing before the Lord, and walked through all the ways of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.22:3: Now in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan, son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe of the temple of the Lord, saying to him,
verses.22:4: "Go to Hilkiah the high priest, so that the money that has been brought into the temple of the Lord may be melted down, which the doorkeepers of the temple have collected from the people,
verses.22:5: and may be given to the craftsmen through the overseers of the house of the Lord, who shall also distribute it to those who work in the temple of the Lord for restoring the structure of the temple,
verses.22:6: namely, to the carpenters and the masons, and to those who mend what is broken, and so that timber and stones from the quarries may be bought to restore the temple of the Lord.
verses.22:7: However, let the silver that they receive not be reckoned against them, but let them hold it in their power and in good faith."
verses.22:8: Now Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan, who also read it.
verses.22:9: Shaphan the scribe also came to the king and reported back to him what he had commanded, and said, "Your servants have melted down the money that was found in the house of the Lord, and have given it to be distributed to the craftsmen by the supervisors of the works of the temple of the Lord."
verses.22:10: Shaphan the scribe also told the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." When Shaphan had read it before the king,
verses.22:11: and the king had heard the words of the book of the law of the Lord, he tore his garments.
verses.22:12: And he commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,
verses.22:13: "Go and consult the Lord concerning me, and concerning the people, and concerning all Judah, about the words of this scroll that has been found; for great wrath of the Lord has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, so as to do everything that is written for us."
verses.22:14: Therefore Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, and Achbor, and Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum, son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments, who lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter; and they spoke to her.
verses.22:15: And she answered them, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
verses.22:16: 'This is what the Lord says: Look, I will bring evils upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words of the law that the king of Judah has read,
verses.22:17: because they have abandoned Me and have sacrificed to foreign gods, provoking Me in all the works of their hands; and My indignation will be kindled in this place and will not be extinguished.'
verses.22:18: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to consult the Lord, say this: 'This is what the Lord God of Israel says: Because you heard the words of the scroll,
verses.22:19: and your heart was terrified, and you humbled yourself before the Lord upon hearing the words against this place and its inhabitants, namely, that they would become an astonishment and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before Me; I also have heard, says the Lord:
verses.22:20: therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tomb in peace, so that your eyes will not see all the evils that I am about to bring upon this place.'"
verses.23:1: And they reported to the king what she had said. Then he sent, and all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem were gathered to him.
verses.23:2: And the king went up to the temple of the Lord, and all the men of Judah, and all who lived in Jerusalem with him, the priests and the prophets, and all the people from small to great; and with everyone listening, he read all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the Lord.
verses.23:3: And the king stood upon the step and made a covenant before the Lord, that they would walk after the Lord and keep His precepts and testimonies and ceremonies with all their heart and with their whole soul, and re-establish the words of this covenant that were written in that book; and the people agreed to the covenant.
verses.23:4: And the king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the doorkeepers, to throw out of the temple of the Lord all the vessels that had been made for Baal, and in the grove, and for all the host of heaven; and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the valley of Kidron, and carried their dust to Bethel.
verses.23:5: And he destroyed the soothsayers whom the kings of Judah had appointed to sacrifice at the high places throughout the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those who burned incense to Baal, and to the sun, and to the moon, and to the twelve signs, and to all the host of heaven.
verses.23:6: And he had the grove carried out from the house of the Lord outside Jerusalem in the valley of Kidron, and burned it there, and reduced it to dust, and threw it upon the tombs of the common people.
verses.23:7: He also tore down the small chambers of the effeminate men that were in the house of the Lord, for which the women were weaving, as it were, little houses of the grove.
verses.23:8: And he gathered all the priests from the cities of Judah, and defiled the high places where the priests used to sacrifice, from Geba to Beersheba; and he tore down the altars of the gates at the entrance of the doorway of Joshua, the governor of the city, which was on the left side of the gate of the city.
verses.23:9: Nevertheless, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but only ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
verses.23:10: He also defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, so that no one would consecrate his son or daughter through fire to Molech.
verses.23:11: He also removed the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the temple of the Lord, next to the chamber of Nathan-melech the eunuch, who was in Pharurim; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
verses.23:12: The king also tore down the altars that were on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the temple of the Lord; and he ran from there and scattered their ashes into the Kidron brook.
verses.23:13: The king also polluted the high places that were in Jerusalem, on the right side of the mountain of offense, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth, the idol of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh, the offense of Moab, and for Milcom, the abomination of the sons of Ammon.
verses.23:14: And he shattered the statues and cut down the groves, and filled their places with the bones of the dead.
verses.23:15: Moreover, as for the altar that was in Bethel and the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made: both that altar and the high place he tore down, and burned, and crushed to dust, and he also set fire to the grove.
verses.23:16: And Josiah turned and saw there the tombs that were on the mountain; and he sent and took the bones from the tombs, and burned them upon the altar, and polluted it according to the word of the Lord that the man of God spoke, who had foretold these things.
verses.23:17: And he said, "What is that monument that I see?" And the citizens of that city answered him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and foretold these things that you have done upon the altar of Bethel."
verses.23:18: And he said, "Leave him alone; let no one disturb his bones." And his bones remained untouched, along with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
verses.23:19: Moreover, Josiah removed all the shrines of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord, and he did to them according to all the deeds that he had done in Bethel.
verses.23:20: And he killed upon the altars all the priests of the high places who were there, and burned human bones upon them; and he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.23:21: And he commanded all the people, saying, "Keep the Passover to the Lord your God, according to what is written in the book of this covenant."
verses.23:22: For no such Passover was kept from the days of the judges who judged Israel, and in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah,
verses.23:23: as this Passover was kept to the Lord in Jerusalem in the eighteenth year of King Josiah.
verses.23:24: Moreover, Josiah removed the mediums and the diviners, and the figures of idols, and the impurities, and the abominations that had been in the land of Judah and Jerusalem, so that he might establish the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in the temple of the Lord.
verses.23:25: Before him there was no king like him who returned to the Lord with all his heart and with his whole soul and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses; nor did anyone like him arise after him.
verses.23:26: Nevertheless, the Lord did not turn away from the anger of His great fury, with which His fury was enraged against Judah because of the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
verses.23:27: Therefore the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from My presence, just as I removed Israel, and I will cast away this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
verses.23:28: Now the rest of the accounts of Josiah, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
verses.23:29: In his days Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the Euphrates River, and King Josiah went out to meet him; and he was killed at Megiddo when he had seen him.
verses.23:30: And his servants carried him dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, and anointed him, and appointed him king in place of his father.
verses.23:31: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.23:32: And he did evil before the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.23:33: And Pharaoh Necho bound him at Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath, so that he would not reign in Jerusalem; and he imposed a fine on the land of one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.23:34: And Pharaoh Necho appointed Eliakim son of Josiah as king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz and led him into Egypt, and he died there.
verses.23:35: Now Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, having assessed the land individually so that it would be contributed according to the command of Pharaoh; and he exacted from each one according to his means, both silver and gold, from the people of the land, so that he might give it to Pharaoh Necho.
verses.23:36: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Zebidah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
verses.23:37: And he did evil before the Lord, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.24:1: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years; and again he rebelled against him.
verses.24:2: And the Lord sent against him raiders of the Chaldeans, and raiders of Syria, and raiders of Moab, and raiders of the sons of Ammon; and He sent them into Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the Lord that He had spoken through His servants the prophets.
verses.24:3: Now this happened through the word of the Lord against Judah, so that He might remove it from before Him because of all the sins of Manasseh that he committed,
verses.24:4: and because of the innocent blood that he shed, and he filled Jerusalem with the blood of the innocent; and on account of this the Lord was not willing to be appeased.
verses.24:5: Now the rest of the accounts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah? And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers,
verses.24:6: and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.
verses.24:7: And the king of Egypt did not go out again from his land, for the king of Babylon had taken, from the stream of Egypt to the Euphrates River, all that had belonged to the king of Egypt.
verses.24:8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: And he did evil before the Lord, according to all that his father had done.
verses.24:10: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon went up against Jerusalem, and the city was surrounded with siege works.
verses.24:11: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city with his servants so that they might attack it.
verses.24:12: And Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon received him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.24:13: And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the royal house, and he cut to pieces all the golden vessels that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.
verses.24:14: And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the strong men of the army, ten thousand, into captivity, and every craftsman and locksmith; and nothing was left, except the poor of the people of the land.
verses.24:15: He also carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his eunuchs; and the judges of the land he led into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.24:16: And all the stalwart men, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and locksmiths, one thousand, all strong men and warriors: the king of Babylon led them captive to Babylon.
verses.24:17: And he appointed Mattaniah his uncle in his place, and gave him the name Zedekiah.
verses.24:18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years of age when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.24:19: And he did evil before the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.24:20: For the Lord was angry against Jerusalem and against Judah, until He cast them away from His presence; and Zedekiah withdrew from the king of Babylon.
verses.25:1: Now it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and they surrounded it and erected fortifications all around it.
verses.25:2: And the city was shut in and encircled with ramparts until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah,
verses.25:3: on the ninth day of the month; and famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.25:4: And the city was breached, and all the fighting men fled at night by the way of the gate that is between the double wall near the king's garden. Meanwhile, the Chaldeans were besieging the city all around. So Zedekiah fled by the way that leads to the plains of the wilderness.
verses.25:5: And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plain of Jericho; and all the warriors who were with him were scattered and left him.
verses.25:6: Therefore, having seized the king, they brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, who spoke judgment with him.
verses.25:7: And he killed the sons of Zedekiah in his presence, and gouged out his eyes, and bound him with chains, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.25:8: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of the king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, commander of the army, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.25:9: And he set fire to the house of the Lord and the house of the king; and he burned up the houses of Jerusalem and every house with fire.
verses.25:11: Now Nebuzaradan, commander of the forces, carried away the remaining part of the people that had stayed in the city, and the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the common people.
verses.25:12: And from the poor of the land he left vinedressers and farmers.
verses.25:13: Now the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the temple of the Lord, and the bases, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and carried away all the bronze to Babylon.
verses.25:14: They also took the bronze pots, and the scoops, and the three-pronged forks, and the cups, and the small mortars, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered.
verses.25:15: Moreover, the commander of the forces took the censers and the bowls, those that were of gold as gold, and those that were of silver as silver,
verses.25:16: that is, the two pillars, the one sea, and the bases that Solomon had made in the temple of the Lord; the bronze of all the vessels was beyond weight.
verses.25:17: One pillar had a height of eighteen cubits, and a bronze capital upon it three cubits in height, and latticework and pomegranates upon the capital of the pillar, all of bronze; and the second pillar also had similar adornment.
verses.25:18: The commander of the forces also took Seraiah the first priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and three doorkeepers.
verses.25:19: And from the city he took one eunuch who was set over the fighting men, and five men from those who had stood before the king, whom he found in the city, and Sopher, commander of the army, who examined the recruits from the people of the land, and sixty men from the common people who had been found in the city.
verses.25:20: Taking them, Nebuzaradan, commander of the soldiers, brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
verses.25:21: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath; and Judah was carried away from its land.
verses.25:22: Now over the people who had been left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left behind, he set Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.
verses.25:23: And when all the leaders of the soldiers heard this, they and the men who were with them, namely, that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their companions.
verses.25:24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their companions, saying, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans; remain in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you."
verses.25:25: Now it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came, and ten men with him, and they struck down Gedaliah, so that he died, as well as the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.25:26: And all the people, from the small to the great, and the commanders of the soldiers rose up and came into Egypt, fearing the Chaldeans.
verses.25:27: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year in which he had begun to reign, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
verses.25:28: And he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.25:29: And he changed his garments, which he had worn in prison, and he ate bread continually in his presence all the days of his life.
verses.25:30: He also appointed an allowance for him without interruption, which was indeed given to him by the king day by day, all the days of his life.

notes.1:2: The Vulgate uses the form Beelzebub (as in the New Testament; compare Hebrew Baal-zebub), and reads literally "whether I can live from this illness of mine" (vivere queam de infirmitate mea hac), meaning survive or recover.
notes.1:8: Latin vir pilosus literally means "a hairy man," rendering a Hebrew idiom that can refer either to a hairy body or to a cloak of coarse hair.
notes.1:12: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "the fire of God," the Clementine Vulgate reads simply "fire" (ignis).
notes.1:13: The Vulgate renders the captain's plea negatively as "do not despise my life" (noli despicere animam meam) and in v. 14 as "have mercy on my life" (miserearis animae meae), where the Hebrew reads "let my life be precious in your sight."
notes.1:17: The Clementine Vulgate explicitly identifies Joram as "his brother" (frater ejus), a detail absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.2:3: Here and in v. 5, the Vulgate reads simply "from you" (a te), omitting the Hebrew idiom "from over your head."
notes.2:9: Latin duplex spiritus tuus literally means "your double spirit," reflecting the Hebrew legal idiom for the firstborn son's double inheritance share.
notes.2:12: The Vulgate renders the title in the singular as "its charioteer" (auriga ejus), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the plural "its horsemen."
notes.2:14: In a notable Vulgate reading shared with the Septuagint tradition, Elisha strikes the Jordan twice—first unsuccessfully ("and they were not divided") before calling out "Where is the God of Elijah even now?" (omitting "the Lord" of the Hebrew)—whereas the Hebrew text records a single strike.
notes.2:24: The Vulgate reads simply "two bears" (duo ursi), without specifying female bears as in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.3:8: The Vulgate uses the Greco-Latin regional name Idumea (Idumaeae) here, whereas it uses Edom in vv. 9, 12, 20, and 26.
notes.3:21: Latin accincti erant balteo desuper literally means "were belted with a sword belt from above" (a baldric worn over the shoulder), rendering the Hebrew idiom for everyone from the youngest age able to put on armor and upward.
notes.3:23: The Vulgate reads "It is blood of the sword" (Sanguis gladii est), taking the Hebrew verb form for "surely destroyed" as the similar-looking noun for "sword."
notes.3:25: Where the Hebrew names the Moabite stronghold Kir-hareseth, the Vulgate interprets the name etymologically as "the clay walls" (muri ... fictiles).
notes.3:27: Latin in Israel can mean either "in Israel" (outrage felt among the Israelites) or "against Israel" (wrath coming upon Israel); the exact cause and nature of this indignation remain debated.
notes.4:2: The Vulgate reads "with which to anoint myself" (quo ungar), interpreting the Hebrew term for an oil flask from the verbal root meaning "to anoint."
notes.4:16: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew seasonal idiom as "if life accompanies us" (si vita comes fuerit) and reads "you will have a son in your womb" (habebis in utero filium) where the Hebrew has "you will embrace a son."
notes.4:23: The Vulgate reads "I will go" (Vadam) rather than the Hebrew greeting "Peace" (meaning "It is well").
notes.4:35: The Vulgate reads "yawned" (oscitavit) where the Hebrew text has "sneezed."
notes.4:41: The Vulgate specifies "bitterness" (amaritudinis), matching the bitter colocynth gourds of 4:39, where the Hebrew has "harmful thing."
notes.5:1: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom for a mighty warrior with two adjectives, "mighty and wealthy" (fortis et dives).
notes.5:18: In the Vulgate, Naaman explicitly asks Elisha to intercede for him ("about which you should plead with the Lord for your servant"), whereas the Hebrew expresses a direct wish for the Lord's pardon.
notes.5:19: The Vulgate reads "in the choice season of the earth" (electo terræ tempore), interpreting the obscure Hebrew phrase for "some distance of land" as a reference to the prime season of the year.
notes.5:24: The Vulgate reads "already in the evening" (jam vesperi), taking the Hebrew word for "the hill" (Ophel) as a term for twilight or dusk.
notes.5:26: The Vulgate renders this clause as a declarative accusation ("Now therefore you have accepted silver, and you have accepted garments...") rather than the Hebrew rhetorical question ("Is it a time to accept money and garments...?").
notes.6:2: Vulgate specifies "from the forest" (Latin de silva) as the source of the timber, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from there."
notes.6:8: Vulgate reads "let us set an ambush" (Latin ponamus insidias; similarly "in ambush" in 6:9), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "my camp will be."
notes.6:10: Vulgate reads "occupied it beforehand" (Latin praeoccupavit eum) with the king of Israel as subject, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text states that the man of God warned him.
notes.6:22: Vulgate renders this clause as a negative statement, "for you did not capture them with your sword and bow" (Latin neque enim cepisti eos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text frames it as a rhetorical question.
notes.6:27: Vulgate gives an indicative statement, "The Lord does not save you" (Latin Non te salvat Dominus), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is conditional ("If the Lord does not help you").
notes.7:1: Latin modius ("measure") is a Roman dry measure of roughly nine liters (about a peck), and stater is a Greco-Roman silver coin; the Vulgate uses these to render the Hebrew seah and shekel.
notes.7:11: Vulgate reads "went" (Latin Ierunt) for the gatekeepers' action, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "called out."
notes.7:13: Vulgate streamlines a difficult, repetitive parenthetical clause in the Hebrew Masoretic Text into "(because only they are left in the entire multitude of Israel, for the others have been consumed)."
notes.7:14: Vulgate reads simply "two horses" (Latin duos equos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "two chariots with horses."
notes.8:2: The Vulgate reads "for many days" (diebus multis), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew text reads "seven years."
notes.8:10: The Vulgate reads "You will be healed" (Sanaberis), aligning with the Hebrew Qere and Septuagint, whereas the written Hebrew text (Ketiv) reads "You will not live."
notes.8:11: The critical text prints Stetique (literally "and I stood"), evidently for Stetitque ("and he stood"), which the third-person narrative requires; the Vulgate also reads "was troubled to the flushing of his face" (conturbatus est usque ad suffusionem vultus), where the Hebrew reads "fixed his gaze until he was ashamed."
notes.8:16: The Vulgate coordinates both kings in the genitive ("of Joram... and of Jehoshaphat king of Judah"), reflecting a difficult chronological clause in the Hebrew.
notes.8:23: "The book of the words of the days" (libro verborum dierum) literally translates the Hebrew idiom for the royal chronicles or annals.
notes.9:13: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "on the bare steps" as "in the likeness of a tribunal" (in similitudinem tribunalis), depicting a raised seat of authority.
notes.9:14: The Vulgate reads "had besieged" (obsederat), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "had been guarding" (or defending); similarly, in 9:17-19 the Vulgate reads "chariot" (currum) where the Hebrew reads "horseman."
notes.9:27: The Vulgate reads "Gaver," a distinct place-name form corresponding to "Gur" in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.9:32: The Vulgate reads "Who is this woman?" (Quae est ista?), differing from the Masoretic Hebrew "Who is on my side? Who?"
notes.9:37: The Vulgate renders the closing clause as a question asked by passersby ("so that those passing by will say, 'Is this that Jezebel?'"), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads negatively, "so that no one can say, 'This is Jezebel.'"
notes.10:9: Vulgate 'si ego conjuravi' ("if I conspired") frames Jehu's admission as a rhetorical conditional, whereas the Hebrew reads "look, I conspired."
notes.10:12: Vulgate 'Cameram pastorum' ("the Chamber of the Shepherds") renders the Hebrew place name Beth-eked of the Shepherds (literally "house of binding/shearing of the shepherds").
notes.10:24: Vulgate mirrors the compressed Hebrew idiom ('anima ejus ... pro anima illius'), meaning that the life of whichever guard lets a captive escape will answer for the escapee's life.
notes.10:25: Vulgate 'civitatem templi Baal' ("the city of the temple of Baal") literally renders the Hebrew expression for the inner citadel or sanctuary precinct of Baal's temple; in 10:26 the Vulgate also reads singular 'statuam' ("statue") where the Hebrew has plural pillars.
notes.10:32: Vulgate 'coepit Dominus taedere super Israel' ("the Lord began to grow weary of Israel") reflects a distinct reading of the Hebrew verb, where the Masoretic Text reads "began to cut off [territory] in Israel."
notes.11:2: Vulgate 'furata est eum ... et nutricem ejus de triclinio' ("stole him ... and his nurse from the bedchamber") treats the bedchamber as the place from which the nurse was taken, whereas the Hebrew states that Jehosheba hid Joash and his nurse in the bedchamber.
notes.11:6: Vulgate 'domus Messa' ("the house of Messa") treats the rare Hebrew term 'massah' ("barrier" or "defense") as a proper name, and renders the Hebrew "runners/guards" here and in 11:19 as 'scutarii' ("shield-bearers").
notes.11:8: Vulgate 'septum templi' ("the enclosure of the temple," also plural in 11:15) renders Hebrew 'sederot' ("ranks"), understanding the boundary as the temple precinct rather than the soldiers' lines.
notes.11:14: Vulgate reads 'super tribunal' ("on the platform") and 'cantores' ("the singers") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "by the pillar" and "the captains" (reflecting a different Hebrew vocalization).
notes.11:19: Vulgate 'Cerethi et Phelethi legiones' ("the legions of the Cherethites and Pelethites") identifies the royal guard with David's famed corps, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Carites and the guards."
notes.12:5: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew assessment phrase literally as "by those who pass by" (a praetereuntibus) and "for the price of a soul" (pro pretio animae), referring to temple offerings and redemption dues.
notes.12:6: Latin juxta ordinem suum ("according to their order," also in 12:8) differs from the Hebrew ("from his acquaintance"). The compound sartatecta (literally "mended and roofed," vv. 6-9, 13) is a classical Roman architectural term for the structural repairs and upkeep of a building.
notes.12:9: The Vulgate reads prohibiti sunt ("were prohibited"), whereas the Hebrew states that the priests "consented" or "agreed" to the arrangement.
notes.12:11: The Vulgate reads effundebant ("poured out"), depicting the officials emptying the chest to count the money, where the Hebrew verb means "tied up" (in bags).
notes.12:14: The Vulgate specifies hydriae ("water jars"), fuscinulae ("forks"), and thuribula ("censers") where the Hebrew lists basins, snuffers, and sprinkling bowls.
notes.13:6: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew "Asherah" (a cultic wooden pole or image) as lucus ("sacred grove"), its standard Latin rendering for the term.
notes.13:14: The Vulgate renders the final phrase in the singular as auriga ejus ("its charioteer," as in 2 Kings 2:12), whereas the Hebrew has the plural "its horsemen."
notes.13:18: The Vulgate adds jaculo ("with a dart/arrow"), specifying the instrument used to strike the ground, whereas the Hebrew simply reads "Strike the ground."
notes.13:19: The Vulgate reads quinquies, aut sexies, sive septies ("five times, or six times, or seven times"), adding "or seven times" where the Hebrew mentions only five or six times.
notes.13:23: The Vulgate reads neque projicere penitus ("nor to cast them away completely"), without the Hebrew's "from his presence," and concludes with usque in praesens tempus ("up to the present time").
notes.14:7: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew Valley of Salt as "valle Salinarum" ("Valley of the Salt Pits") and translates the place name Sela as the common noun "petram" ("the rock").
notes.14:13: The Vulgate reads transitively "adduxit eum in Jerusalem" ("brought him to Jerusalem"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text states simply that Joash went to Jerusalem.
notes.14:15: The recurring Vulgate phrase "in libro sermonum [or verborum] dierum" ("in the book of the words of the days") literally renders the Hebrew idiom for royal annals or chronicles, while "verborum" and "sermonum" ("accounts") in this formula cover a king's deeds and affairs.
notes.14:25: The Vulgate splits the Hebrew town name Gath-hepher into two parts, "de Geth, quae est in Opher" ("from Gath, which is in Opher"), and translates the Sea of the Arabah as "mare solitudinis" ("Sea of the Wilderness").
notes.14:26: Latin "usque ad clausos carcere et extremos" ("even to those shut up in prison and the lowest") is Jerome's concrete rendering of a Hebrew idiom meaning "neither bond nor free," that is, no one left at all.
notes.14:28: Latin "Judae" in "restituit Damascum et Emath Judae in Israel" is read here as dative ("to Judah"), matching 14:22, though it can also be taken as genitive ("of Judah," referring to territory that had formerly belonged to Judah).
notes.15:5: Latin "in domo libera seorsum" ("in a free house apart") renders the obscure Hebrew term for an isolated house. The Clementine Vulgate also reads the future tense "judicabit" ("will judge") rather than the imperfect "judicabat" ("was judging"), translated here as "would judge" to fit the past-tense narrative.
notes.15:10: Latin "palam" ("openly") translates the Hebrew phrase "before the people," which some Greek witnesses take as the place name Ibleam.
notes.15:25: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew with "juxta" ("beside Argob and beside Arieh") and puts "quinquaginta viros" ("fifty men") in the accusative as additional victims struck down with Pekahiah, whereas the Hebrew is usually read as fifty Gileadites who accompanied Pekah in the conspiracy.
notes.15:29: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew town name Abel-beth-maacah partly into Latin as "Abel Domum, Maacha" ("Abel House, Maacah," with a comma after "Domum" in the Clementine text, so that Maacha stands as a separate name), and renders the destination as "in Assyrios" ("to the Assyrians").
notes.16:3: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom for child sacrifice doubly as 'consecrated... passing him through the fire' (consecravit, transferens per ignem). It also reads 'idols' (idola) where the Hebrew has 'abominations' of the nations whom the Lord drove out.
notes.16:9: The Vulgate identifies the place of deportation as 'Cyrene' (Cyrenen), whereas the Hebrew text reads Kir.
notes.16:12: The Vulgate reads 'venerated it' (veneratus est illud), whereas the Hebrew states that Ahaz 'approached the altar.'
notes.16:14: The Vulgate reads 'from the place of the altar, and from the place of the temple of the Lord' (de loco altaris, et de loco templi Domini), where the Hebrew reads 'from between the altar and the house of the Lord.'
notes.16:18: The Vulgate retains the untranslated Hebrew term Musach (likely a covered canopy or portico used on the Sabbath) and reads 'turned into the temple of the Lord' (convertit in templum Domini), where the Hebrew is generally understood as removing it from the temple.
notes.17:8: The Vulgate reads 'consumed' (consumpserat) and concludes 'and of the kings of Israel, because they had done likewise' (et regum Israel, quia similiter fecerant), where the Hebrew refers to the customs that the kings of Israel had made.
notes.17:10: Following its consistent idiom, the Vulgate renders the Hebrew sacred pillars and Asherah poles as 'statues and groves' (statuas et lucos).
notes.17:19: The Vulgate reads 'errors' (erroribus) where the Hebrew has 'statutes' or 'customs.'
notes.17:31: The Vulgate reads 'the Hivites' (Hevaei), whereas the Hebrew text reads 'the Avvites' (the inhabitants of Avva, v. 24).
notes.17:32: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew phrase for people of every rank as 'from among the lowest' (de novissimis), referring to priests appointed from the lowest class.
notes.18:4: Vulgate renders the Hebrew sacred pillars as statuas ("statues") and Asherah symbols as lucos ("groves"), and uses the active singular vocavit ("he called") with the Latin transliteration Nohestan (Nehushtan).
notes.18:11: Vulgate reads the plural fluviis Gozan ("the rivers of Gozan"), whereas the Hebrew text has the singular "the river of Gozan," and uses the ethnic plural in Assyrios ("to the Assyrians") for the land of Assyria.
notes.18:16: Vulgate reads confregit ... valvas ... et laminas auri quas ipse affixerat ("broke off the doors ... and the plates of gold that he himself had fastened"), whereas the Hebrew text speaks of stripping gold from the doors and doorposts Hezekiah had overlaid.
notes.18:23: Vulgate reads transite ad dominum meum ("come over to my lord"), diverging from the Hebrew idiom commonly translated "make a wager with my master."
notes.18:31: Vulgate renders the Hebrew idiom "make a blessing [i.e., terms of peace] with me" as Facite mecum quod vobis est utile ("Do with me what is advantageous to you").
notes.19:4: The Vulgate puts argueret ("to reprove") in the imperfect subjunctive coordinated with exprobraret ("to reproach") as part of Rabshakeh's mission, whereas the Hebrew shifts back to God as subject ("and will rebuke the words").
notes.19:9: The Vulgate renders Hebrew Cush as Æthiopia ("Ethiopia") and reads et iret contra eum ("and was going against him") in the temporal clause where the Hebrew has "he returned and sent" (i.e., "sent again").
notes.19:24: The Vulgate connects ego succidi ("I myself have cut down") across the verse break with saltum Carmeli ejus ("the forest of its Carmel") in v. 23, and renders Hebrew "streams of Egypt" literally as aquas clausas ("enclosed waters").
notes.19:25: The Vulgate reads in ruinam collium pugnantium ("a ruin of fighting hills"), translating the Hebrew phrase for "ruinous heaps" literally as "hills" (collium) and "fighting" (pugnantium).
notes.19:35: The Vulgate uses singular verbs (surrexisset, "he had risen"; vidit, "he saw") pointing forward to Sennacherib in v. 36, whereas the Hebrew uses plural ("when they arose early").
notes.19:37: The Vulgate reads in terram Armeniorum ("into the land of the Armenians") where the Hebrew has "into the land of Ararat."
notes.20:5: The Vulgate uses the perfect tense sanavi te ("I have healed you") where the Hebrew has a participle ("I am going to heal you"), and renders "house of the Lord" as templum Domini ("temple of the Lord," also in v. 8).
notes.20:11: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew "steps of Ahaz" as in horologio Achaz ("on the sundial of Ahaz"), distinguishing between lineæ ("lines") and gradus ("degrees") in vv. 9-11.
notes.20:13: The Vulgate reads Lætatus est autem in adventu eorum ("rejoiced at their arrival"), aligning with Isaiah 39:2 and the Septuagint where the Masoretic Text of 2 Kings has "he listened to them."
notes.20:19: The Vulgate renders Hezekiah's closing words as a direct wish, sit pax et veritas in diebus meis ("let there be peace and truth in my days"), without the rhetorical question "is it not [good] if..." found in the Hebrew.
notes.21:2: The Vulgate reads idola ("idols") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "abominations."
notes.21:3: Latin lucos ("groves," and singular luci in 21:7) is the Vulgate's regular rendering of the Hebrew Asherah cult objects as sacred groves, here given in the plural rather than the Hebrew singular.
notes.21:11: Latin immunditiis ("impurities," also in 21:21) is the Vulgate's literal derogatory term for idols, corresponding to Hebrew gillulim.
notes.21:13: Whereas the Hebrew text compares Jerusalem to a dish wiped clean and turned upside down, the Vulgate renders the image as wax writing tablets (tabulae) erased by turning and drawing the stylus (stylum) repeatedly over their face.
notes.21:17: The Clementine Vulgate reads ut ("such as") before universa quae fecit where the Hebrew has "and"; sermonum ("words") here and in 21:25 reflects the Vulgate's literal rendering of Hebrew debarim ("words/matters"), including the chronicle title libro sermonum dierum ("book of the words of the days").
notes.22:3: The Vulgate construes templi Domini as a genitive modifying scribam ("the scribe of the temple of the Lord"), whereas the Hebrew text takes "to the house of the Lord" as the destination to which Shaphan was sent.
notes.22:4: Both here (confletur) and in 22:9 (conflaverunt), the Vulgate speaks of melting down the temple money, whereas the Hebrew refers to counting or pouring out the silver; in 22:5, sartatecta is a classical Latin architectural term (literally "things patched and roofed") denoting the structural fabric and upkeep of a building.
notes.22:12: The Vulgate preserves the shorter proper name Micha ("Micah") where the Hebrew text reads "Micaiah."
notes.22:19: The Vulgate reads perterritum est ("was terrified") where the Hebrew text reads "was tender/soft"; similarly, the Vulgate reads verba legis ("words of the law") in 22:16 and verba voluminis ("words of the scroll") in 22:18.
notes.22:20: The Vulgate ends 22:20 here with Huldah's oracle, without the closing clause ("and they brought word back to the king") found at the end of this verse in the Hebrew text.
notes.23:1: In the Clementine Vulgate, the opening sentence ("And they reported to the king what she had said") begins 23:1, whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text it concludes 22:20.
notes.23:4: Here and throughout the chapter (vv. 6, 7, 14, 15), the Vulgate renders Hebrew Asherah (a wooden cultic image or pole) as lucus ("grove"), following the Septuagint; in v. 4 it also reads "in the grove" (in luco).
notes.23:5: Vulgate "soothsayers" (aruspices) renders a Hebrew term for idolatrous priests, and "the twelve signs" (duodecim signis) specifies the twelve signs of the zodiac where the Hebrew reads "constellations" (mazzalot).
notes.23:11: Vulgate "in Pharurim" treats the obscure Hebrew term parwarim ("precincts" or "colonnades") as a proper name, and its masculine relative pronoun (qui) attaches Pharurim to Nathan-melech rather than to the chamber.
notes.23:12: Vulgate "and he ran from there" (et cucurrit inde) reflects an alternate vocalization of the Hebrew verb usually understood as "and he crushed them there."
notes.24:5: In the Clementine Vulgate, "And Jehoiakim slept with his fathers" ends 24:5, leaving only "and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place" as 24:6, whereas the Hebrew text places both clauses in 24:6.
notes.24:14: Vulgate "locksmith" (clusorem, also in v. 16) is a literal coinage from Latin claudere ("to shut/lock") for the Hebrew term masger, commonly rendered "smiths" or "metalworkers."
notes.24:15: Vulgate "judges of the land" (judices terrae) renders a Hebrew phrase usually understood as "chief men" or "mighty men of the land."
notes.25:6: "spoke judgment with him" renders the literal Latin idiom (locutus est cum eo judicium) for passing judicial sentence upon someone.
notes.25:9: The Vulgate reads omnemque domum ("and every house"), without the word "great" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("every great house").
notes.25:16: The Vulgate connects this verse to v. 15 with id est ("that is"), making the bronze furnishings accusative objects of what the commander took; "was beyond weight" translates the literal Latin non erat pondus ("there was no weight").
notes.25:19: Where the Hebrew text has the title "the scribe" (hassopher) of the army commander who mustered the people, the Vulgate treats Sopher as a proper name in apposition to "commander of the army" and uses Roman military terminology (probabat tyrones) for examining recruits.
notes.25:24: The Vulgate reads servire Chaldaeis ("to serve the Chaldeans"), taking the Hebrew word as an infinitive ("from serving") rather than the Masoretic Text's noun "the servants/officials of the Chaldeans."
